National Syndicalism.d: Workers and employers belong together in national syndicates, because each trade is best run through unions of producers that manage their own sector under the state (Syndicalism). Society is organized into corporate groups of labour and employers who cooperate by function and not by class, which gives every trade a voice and a purpose (Corporatism). The state is the highest moral authority and ethical entity of the nation, because it unites individuals in a spiritual organization that realizes their ultimate ends (Ethical Statism). The nation is a living spiritual community with its own soul, heroic past and folklore, so that unity of the people stands above class (Romantic Nationalism). Merit and technical hierarchy in management of worker-owned corporations give production its order, since a trained elite leads each sector for the nation (Hierarchical Communism). Modern industry and science are embraced to strengthen the traditional nation, by placing machines in the service of heritage and romantic ideals (Reactionary Modernism). Civilian life is mobilized and drilled in national service, so that every worker takes part in discipline and shared duty (Regimentalism). Because delegates are chosen through trade syndicates and professional guilds, the country is governed by producers rather than by districts (Syndicracy). Parties that compete in elections and pass laws on behalf of voters are rejected, since they divide the nation into quarrelling factions (against Representative Democracy). An economy without state direction, left to private transactions, is rejected because competition among private interests would divide the nation (against Laissez-Faire). Central planning and state ownership of production by officials are rejected, since they replace the producers' own organization with bureaucracy (against State Socialism). A revolution that abolishes classes and money at once is rejected, because it would break the national community into warring camps (against Communization). Individual rights set against the community are rejected because liberal freedom of the press and of expression has meaning only inside the nation that gives it a place (against Civil Liberalism). The belief that all human beings form one community beyond national borders is rejected, because loyalties belong first to the people's own nation (against Cosmopolitanism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is rejected, since it subordinates the nation's interests to a joint order (against Internationalism).

Brazilian Integralism.d: Society is organized into corporate groups of family, municipality and profession, because their common functions, rather than class interests, make the nation an integral whole under guidance (Corporatism). Public and moral life is subordinated to revealed doctrine and church authority, since God, Fatherland and Family rest on a confessional orthodoxy (Religious Traditionalism). The ruler upholds religion and unifies the people as its defender against dissent, so that the spiritual order of the nation is kept (Religious Authoritarianism). The nation is defined by shared culture, language, traditions and heritage rather than ancestry, since one spirit unites citizens of every descent (Cultural Nationalism). A unitary state concentrates legislative and administrative authority in the national government, because a single strong direction must enforce the same order uniformly in every province (Centralism). Rights and choices set against the state are rejected, since individual freedom of the press and expression dissolves the moral bonds of family and nation (against Civil Liberalism). Free private transactions without national direction are rejected because they set individual profit above the common good (against Laissez-Faire). Central planning and state ownership of production are rejected, since officials would replace the family and the corporations in running the economy (against State Socialism). A revolution that abolishes classes, money and religion is rejected because it destroys the family and denies God (against Communization). Parties and elected representatives who pass laws on behalf of voters are rejected, because they divide the people instead of expressing the nation as a whole (against Representative Democracy). Defining the nation by race and its purity is rejected, since the bond of the nation is spirit and not blood (against Racial Nationalism).

Italian Fascism.d: The state absorbs the individual, because every family allegiance, private concern and inner conscience is wholly subordinate to the nation, leaving no private sphere outside it (Totalism). The state is an ethical and spiritual entity, an organic whole that unites individuals in a higher moral purpose which realizes their ultimate ends (Ethical Statism). Workers and employers are joined in corporate groups under state guidance, so that cooperation by function replaces the struggle between classes (Corporatism). The nation is a living community of tradition, heroic myth and ancestral soul, whose destiny gives its people a purpose beyond themselves (Romantic Nationalism). A strong nation must extend its power over other territories through force and empire, since greatness is shown by dominance and expansion (Imperialism). Authority is concentrated in the national government, because a unitary state enforces one will uniformly over all provinces and sub-national divisions (Centralism). One party dominates the political process and the state apparatus, so that it directs the whole nation rather than competing representatives (Partocracy). One leader holds absolute power without external legal restraints, since decisive personal command is necessary to carry out the national will (Autocracy). Voting for elected representatives who govern on behalf of citizens is rejected, because it splits the nation into quarrelling parties (against Representative Democracy). Direct votes on laws through referendums are rejected, since the crowd is not fit to decide the state's ends (against Referendum Democracy). Safeguarding personal privacy and freedom of speech against the state is rejected, because individual rights cannot stand above the nation (against Civil Libertarianism). Consensual adult conduct and private vices are not exempt from the state, which rejects moral neutrality because lifestyle choices shape the national character (against Permissivism). Free private transactions without government intervention are rejected since the economy must serve national power (against Laissez-Faire). State ownership run by central planning is rejected, because it ends private profit through class doctrine instead of through national unity (against State Socialism). An immediate abolition of the state and classes by revolution is rejected, since the nation must stay above class (against Communization). Belonging to a single community of all human beings is rejected, because loyalty belongs to the nation and its morality does not transcend borders (against Cosmopolitanism). Cooperation among nations through treaties is rejected since the national interest cannot be bound by joint commitments (against Internationalism). Avoiding alliances and wars is rejected because a vigorous state should take part in wars of expansion (against Non-Interventionism). Disarmament and nonviolent resistance are rejected, since war and militarism are instruments of statecraft that make a people strong (against Pacifism). Order kept by peer accountability and ostracism through community trust networks is rejected, because only the state's police and law enforce discipline (against Reputationalism). Splitting territory into many seceding city-states is rejected, since the nation must remain one sovereign whole (against Patchwork). Fluid, spontaneous association without permanent institutions is rejected because fixed structures and formal organization give the nation its form (against Anti-Organizationalism).

Evolianism.d: The highest authority is a single primordial tradition and its sacred metaphysical hierarchy, which affirms an ancient wisdom shared by the civilizations of the past, since spirit stands above matter (Perennial Traditionalism). Power belongs to a distinguished ruling class of inherited status and education, whose warrior honour and long-term stake in the land qualify it to rule (Aristocracy). The medieval order of lords, vassals and personal loyalty bound by land is admired because it joined the sacred to military service (Feudalism). A return to a previous political state of society is sought, because modern developments are a decline that must be undone (Reactionaryism). Rule by the elected representatives of equal voters is rejected, since the numbers of the crowd cannot judge what is highest (against Representative Democracy). The belief in advance through science and reform is rejected, because it mistakes the loss of tradition for improvement of the human condition (against Progressivism). Using government and social action to remedy inequality and discrimination is rejected, since equality denies natural rank (against Social-Progressivism). The protection of individual rights and expression against any authority is rejected because it frees persons from the duty and order that give them a place (against Civil Liberalism). Free markets where profit and trade govern are rejected since commerce stands below honour and service (against Laissez-Faire). State ownership managed centrally for material production is rejected, because it builds society on matter instead of spirit (against State Socialism). A revolution abolishing classes and money is rejected since it destroys every hierarchy and sacred rank (against Communization). An ethic without fixed commandments, resting only on desire, is rejected because a person without a rule has no form (against Amoralism). Unrestrained majority rule driven by mass passions is rejected since it hands power to the lowest elements of society (against Ochlocracy).

Futurism.d: Speed, large-scale manufacturing and machines are the beauty of the age, because industry maximizes energy, infrastructure and material abundance for a people (Industrialism). Humanity should achieve total mastery over nature through technology, so that scarcity and old limits are overcome by human will (Prometheanism). A path to modernity of its own, outside the status quo and distinct from the dominant model, is needed because the new age must break with museums and the past (Alternative Modernism). A vigorous nation extends its power and dominance over other territories through force, since daring shows itself by expansion (Imperialism). Practices, institutions and accumulated wisdom that resist rapid change are rejected because they hold back the restless advance of the new (against Conservatism). Inherited customs and local piety are rejected since reverence for the past blocks the energy of the present (against Traditionalist Conservatism). A return to a previous political order is rejected because the future cannot be reached by looking backward (against Reactionaryism). Dismantling technological civilization to return to wild hunter-gatherer life is rejected, since it would give up the machine that makes the age great (against Primitivism). Opposing automated, hyper-industrial expansion in favour of local craft is rejected, because slow human-scale labour would hold back production and speed (against Neo-Luddism). Repairable, small-scale tools kept to personal creativity and local autonomy are rejected since a gentle, decentralized technology cannot match the power of large machines (against Convivialism).

National-Socialism.d: The individual is wholly absorbed into the national community, because family, conscience and every private allegiance are subordinate to the state (Totalism). All authority is concentrated in the capital, which suppresses regional autonomy and distinctions by complete uniformity, since a single unified will must rule the Reich (Hypercentralism). One leader holds absolute power without external restraint, because the people's will is embodied personally in him (Autocracy). The nation is a community of blood defined by race, so that preservation of its purity and dominance is the goal of politics (Racial Nationalism). All who are related by language and descent should be united into one nation across existing borders, since a people must not be divided (Pan-Nationalism). The nation expands by force over other territories to gain living space, because a strong people has a right to dominance (Imperialism). The state exerts strong directive influence over investment, plans and industry, so that the economy serves the people rather than private profit (Dirigisme). The state is the highest moral and spiritual entity, an ethical whole that unites individuals in one purpose realized through the party and its leader (Ethical Statism). Modern industry, science and technology are embraced to strengthen the heritage of the people, by combining romantic myth with advanced power (Reactionary Modernism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process against the state is rejected, because individual rights cannot restrain the national community (against Civil Libertarianism). Consensual lifestyle choices and personal vices are not private, since the health and character of the people are the state's concern (against Permissivism). Free private transactions without state intervention are rejected because the economy must serve the nation's strength (against Laissez-Faire). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected since freedom of the individual dissolves the unity of the people (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who govern on behalf of voters are rejected because parliamentary parties divide the nation (against Representative Democracy). State ownership of production by class-based planning is rejected, since the national community, not the class, is the unit of the economy (against State Socialism). Immediate abolition of the state, money and classes by revolution is rejected because it dissolves the nation into class struggle (against Communization). Belonging to one human community that transcends national and racial boundaries is rejected, because morality is bound to the people (against Cosmopolitanism). Cooperation among nations for the common good is rejected since treaties and common bodies limit the sovereign power of the nation (against Internationalism). Disarmament and nonviolent settlement are rejected, because war and militarism are instruments through which a people secures its existence (against Pacifism). Coexisting communities recognized with their own customs are rejected since a single people cannot share one state with other races (against Multiculturalism). Many overlapping private jurisdictions competing for members are rejected, because one sovereign state must hold law and force (against Polycentrism). Order kept by trust networks and ostracism instead of police is rejected since the state must command discipline (against Reputationalism). Handling matters at the lowest competent authority is rejected because decisions belong to the central leadership (against Subsidiarity). Splitting the territory into many seceding sovereign city-states is rejected, since the Reich must remain a single territory (against Patchwork). Fluid, spontaneous association without permanent institutions is rejected, because fixed structure and organization carry the will of the people (against Anti-Organizationalism).

Neo-Nazism.d: A postwar revival holds that the nation is defined by race and descent, since preserving the purity of one race is the first duty of politics (Racial Nationalism). The state should absorb the family, conscience and every private allegiance, because a people can survive only when no private sphere stands outside its will (Totalism). Decision-making is concentrated wholly in the capital, with uniformity suppressing regional autonomy and district distinctions, so that the movement rules with one voice (Hypercentralism). A single leader exercises absolute power unrestrained by external law, because the race needs a person who embodies its will (Autocracy). The state is an organic ethical entity that unites individuals and transcends them, so that its moral authority is the highest (Ethical Statism). Personal privacy and free speech safeguarded against the state are rejected since they protect enemies of the race (against Civil Libertarianism). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because liberal freedom dissolves the community of blood (against Civil Liberalism). Voting for elected representatives who govern on behalf of citizens is rejected, since parliaments are run by parties that betray the people (against Representative Democracy). State ownership of production run by central planning is rejected because it serves class and not race (against State Socialism). A revolution that dissolves classes and the state is rejected since it ignores the bond of race (against Communization). A single community of all human beings with shared morality is rejected, because peoples differ by descent and loyalties cannot transcend them (against Cosmopolitanism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions is rejected, since it weakens the sovereignty of the race (against Internationalism). Recognizing coexisting communities with separate customs inside one state is rejected because it mixes peoples and breaks forced unity (against Multiculturalism). Many overlapping competing private jurisdictions are rejected since a single state must hold law over its people (against Polycentrism). Order kept by peer ostracism and trust networks rather than police is rejected because only state force secures the race (against Reputationalism). Handling matters at the lowest competent authority is rejected since decisions belong to the central leadership (against Subsidiarity). Splitting territory into seceding micronations and city-states is rejected because the homeland must remain whole (against Patchwork). Fluid, spontaneous association without fixed institutions is rejected, since permanent structure carries the movement's discipline (against Anti-Organizationalism).

Agrarian Fascism.d: Human life is centred on farming, land stewardship and rural communities, because decentralized cultivation of the soil rears a people with roots (Agrarianism). Land is redistributed to the peasantry and farmed collectively, since the rural worker, not the city, is the foundation of the nation (Agrarian Socialism). A single strong leader holds absolute power over the countryside, because village life needs decisive personal command (Autocracy). The state is a moral organism that unites individuals and gives the nation its spiritual purpose, so that the peasantry serves it as its highest end (Ethical Statism). The nation is an organic spirit born in folklore and ancestral land, since the soil carries its heroic soul (Romantic Nationalism). Inherited customs, natural obligations and local piety are preserved against rapid modernization, because rural tradition holds communal bonds together (Traditionalist Conservatism). Public etiquette, order and behavioural standards are enforced with discipline, since strength and decorum mark a rural, orderly people (Disciplinarianism). Large-scale manufacturing and urban extraction are rejected because they uproot the peasant and drain the countryside (against Industrialism). Individual rights set against the community are rejected, since urban liberal freedom loosens village bonds (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who legislate on behalf of voters are rejected because city parties do not speak for the farming people (against Representative Democracy). Central ownership of production by planners is rejected, since it would take the land from the peasant family (against State Socialism).

Strasserism.d: Each trade should be governed by its own national guild of craftsmen, because the nationalized key industries need producers who answer to the nation (Guild Socialism). The state arranges industrial sectors so that capital works with labour, because workers' syndicates gain a share in every decision of their sector (Social-Corporatism). Firms pass from private owners to their workers, with skilled managers chosen by merit, so that the national economy is run by those who know it (Hierarchical Communism). The nation is defined by race and descent, because the working people form a community of blood (Racial Nationalism). The state is the nation's conscience, which lifts every citizen above private interest because only in it do people reach their highest duties (Ethical Statism). A market left free of regulation, subsidies and tariffs is rejected, since private transactions without government let profit exploit the worker (against Laissez-Faire). The immediate abolition of the state and classes by revolution is rejected, since it ignores the nation as the frame of social justice (against Communization). The protection of individual rights and expression against the community is rejected because liberal freedom serves property (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who govern on behalf of voters are rejected, since parliamentary parties serve capital and not the workers (against Representative Democracy). A single human community with shared morality that transcends borders is rejected, because the worker's loyalty is to the nation (against Cosmopolitanism). Cooperation among nations through treaties is rejected since the nation's socialism must be built within its own borders (against Internationalism). Coexisting communities with separate customs inside one state are rejected because they break the unity of the people (against Multiculturalism).

Falangism.d: Society is organized into vertical syndicates that join workers and employers, because functional bodies, not classes, express the common interests of producers (Corporatism). Inherited customs, natural obligations and the Catholic piety of the people are preserved, since the nation's historic institutions should resist rapid modernization (Traditionalist Conservatism). The state is the moral unity of the nation, a spiritual entity that unites individuals and realizes a higher common destiny (Ethical Statism). The fatherland is a destiny in history, animated by an ancestral soul and heroic mythology, so that Spain has a universal mission (Romantic Nationalism). The nation extends its influence over other territories through the force of empire, because it has a mission among the peoples of its language and culture (Imperialism). Authority is concentrated in the national government with provinces as administrative divisions, since a unitary state enforces one national order (Centralism). Civilian life is mobilized through mandatory service and youth programs, because discipline directs everyone towards national goals (Regimentalism). Autonomous historical regions with their own parliaments are rejected since separatism fractures the unity of the fatherland (against Regionalism). A union of sovereign regions formed by treaty is rejected, because the nation cannot be a compact of parts that may veto the whole (against Confederalism). Free private transactions without state intervention are rejected since the economy must serve national unity (against Laissez-Faire). The protection of individual rights and freedom of expression is rejected because liberalism isolates the person from the community (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who govern for rival parties are rejected, since parties divide the fatherland (against Representative Democracy). State ownership managed centrally for class interests is rejected because it turns the nation into a class dictatorship (against State Socialism). A revolution to abolish classes and money is rejected, since it breaks the national community (against Communization). Splitting territory into seceding city-states is rejected because the homeland is one and indivisible (against Patchwork).

Sansepolcrismo.d: A tax system whose rate increases as the taxable amount rises shifts the burden toward higher incomes, because heavy taxation of great fortunes limits inequality for the working classes (Progressive Taxation). Advances in science, social organization and reform improve the human condition, so that a new Italy breaks with the old order through land reform and worker representation (Progressivism). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship rather than ethnicity, since every citizen who shares the republic's creed belongs to it (Civic Nationalism). The country should extend its power over other territories as a proletarian nation through force, because expansion answers its claims after the war (Imperialism). A tax in which the rate falls as income rises, through head taxes and payroll caps, is rejected since it burdens workers and spares the rich (against Regressive Taxation).

Ecofascism.d: Nature and wild ecosystems have intrinsic value and must be defended through protected wilderness zones, because the land that bears a people must be kept untouched (Conservationism). Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation and renewable energy is needed, since the nation's soil, water and air are its inheritance (Environmentalism). The nation is defined by ethnicity and shared descent bound to a homeland, so that blood and soil belong together (Ethnic Nationalism). The state is the ethical entity that unites individuals and holds them to duties toward land and people (Ethical Statism). The nation remains apart from the affairs of other countries, because closed borders protect its land from foreign pressure and migration (Isolationism). Large-scale manufacturing and extraction are rejected since industrial growth degrades the land and overruns the biosphere (against Industrialism). Free private transactions without environmental regulation are rejected because the market consumes the nation's natural inheritance (against Laissez-Faire). A single human community beyond national bonds is rejected, since loyalty is owed to the homeland and its soil (against Cosmopolitanism). Free trade and open borders on a global basis are rejected because they bring overpopulation and industrial degradation (against Globalism). The protection of individual rights against the state is rejected, since personal freedom cannot outweigh the survival of the land (against Civil Liberalism). Coexisting communities with separate customs inside one territory are rejected, because ethnic unity is needed to protect the homeland (against Multiculturalism).

Sorelianism.d: Workers' unions seize control of the economy through strikes and direct action, because the general strike carries a myth that heroic producers can manage society (Syndicalism). Merit and technical hierarchy within worker-owned corporations give production its order, since an elite of producers leads by example and discipline (Hierarchical Communism). Free private transactions and competition among capitalists are rejected, since the market makes the bourgeoisie soft and corrupts the producers' energy (against Laissez-Faire). Elected representatives who legislate on behalf of citizens are rejected because parliamentary compromise blunts the workers' will and corrupts their leaders (against Representative Democracy). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected, since liberal humanitarianism weakens the heroic spirit of struggle (against Civil Liberalism). Central planning and state ownership are rejected because a bureaucratic state would end the producers' self-organization and replace it with officials (against State Socialism).

Legionarianism.d: The nation is a community of the Orthodox faith, whose bond of baptism and shared religious tradition defines national identity and cohesion (Religious Nationalism). Public life is subordinated to revealed scripture and the authority of the church, since a spiritual rebirth of the people needs confessional orthodoxy (Religious Traditionalism). A captain who defends the faith leads the movement and is followed in sacrifice, so that religion legitimizes authority against dissent (Religious Authoritarianism). Workers, peasants and professions are grouped in corporate bodies through their common function, because the brotherhood of the nation replaces the competition of classes (Corporatism). Youth are mobilized in disciplined nests and labour camps through mandatory service, so that a new man is formed for national goals (Regimentalism). Power is concentrated in the national government in the capital, since a unified state must hold every province to one purpose (Centralism). A market free of state intervention is rejected because it makes money the master of a people called to sacrifice (against Laissez-Faire). Individual rights and expression set against community are rejected, since liberal freedom loosens faith and discipline (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who govern for rival parties are rejected because they corrupt the nation with intrigue (against Representative Democracy). State ownership with central planning is rejected, since it is built on materialism and officials (against State Socialism). A revolution abolishing classes, money and religion is rejected because it denies God (against Communization). An ethic of desire without fixed commandments is rejected since the moral law comes from the church (against Amoralism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason and human dignity without revelation is rejected, because the nation's morality springs from faith (against Secular Humanism).

Peronism.d: The state steers investment and plans industry with strong directive influence, because economic independence needs a national economy that is led and not left alone (Dirigisme). Labour is organized by sectors within a national movement under state guidance, since social justice requires that workers' syndicates cooperate with employers (Social-Corporatism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward the wealthy, so that the fruits of production are shared with those who create them (Progressive Taxation). The state protects the health, habits and living conditions of citizens through benefits and guidance, because a caring leader secures the dignity of the poor (Civic Paternalism). The country avoids alliances and wars that do not concern its defence, since political sovereignty means choosing its own path (Non-Interventionism). The nation is defined by shared culture, language, traditions and heritage, because its popular identity draws on the country's own history (Cultural Nationalism). A free market without regulation or national direction is rejected since private profit would subordinate the nation to foreign capital (against Laissez-Faire). Class-struggle revolution that abolishes the state and money is rejected, because social harmony between capital and labour is the Third Position (against Communization).

Techno-Fascism.d: Advanced technology should enhance human intellect and life through cybernetics and genetic engineering, because the strong nation must raise its people beyond biological limits (Transhumanism). Industrial power and modern science are used to strengthen and protect the nation's heritage, since a romantic past is defended by the most advanced means (Reactionary Modernism). Corporations of firms and workers are organized by function under national guidance, so that technical groups cooperate in place of competing classes (Corporatism). The state is the ethical organism that unites individuals, which holds the highest authority over how the technology of the age is used (Ethical Statism). The nation is held together by shared culture, language and tradition, because a technological people still needs a common heritage (Cultural Nationalism). The country extends its power and dominance over other territories by force and technical superiority, since empire proves its vigour (Imperialism). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because personal freedom would slow the national project (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who pass laws on behalf of voters are rejected, since parliamentary delay cannot match the pace of technical power (against Representative Democracy).

National Solidarity.d: Workers organize in unions that negotiate profit-sharing with business groups, because a business shared with its employees makes class warfare pointless and keeps labour loyal to the nation (Yellow Socialism). One strong leader holds personal authority above rival factions, since a single will can reconcile employers and workers (Autocracy). The nation is defined by common culture, language and heritage, so that solidarity among its members rests on shared traditions (Cultural Nationalism). An economy left to private competition is rejected because unchecked markets set employers against workers (against Laissez-Faire). Revolution aimed at abolishing classes and money is rejected, since the red movement divides the people and ends in tyranny (against Communization). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because liberal individualism isolates the person from the national community (against Civil Liberalism).

Clerical Fascism.d: Economic life is organized into corporate bodies of employers and workers under state direction, because cooperation by function replaces class conflict in a society guided by the church (Corporatism). The church's doctrine is the moral and legal basis of the state, since public and moral life must submit to revealed religion and orthodoxy (Religious Traditionalism). A single leader holds power as the defender of the faith, so that religious legitimacy crushes dissent and unifies society (Religious Authoritarianism). The nation is defined by its religion, because the faith of the majority binds citizens and gives its culture cohesion (Religious Nationalism). Unrestrained markets are rejected since private greed contradicts the church's social teaching (against Laissez-Faire). Liberal freedoms and individual rights are rejected because they let each person defy religious authority (against Civil Liberalism). Parliamentary party politics is rejected, since elected representatives weaken the unity of believers (against Representative Democracy). Class-struggle communism is rejected because it is atheist and sets citizens against each other (against Communization). An ethic of personal desire without commandments is rejected, since moral law has a divine source (against Amoralism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason, not revelation, is rejected because it removes God from public life (against Secular Humanism).

Rexism.d: Society is organized in corporate bodies of the professions and trades, because Christian social teaching puts cooperation by function above class opposition (Corporatism). Public life is subordinated to the doctrine of the Catholic church, since Christ the King is the source of moral order (Religious Traditionalism). A leader, as the defender of Catholic faith, holds authority and silences dissent, so that the church and the state stand together (Religious Authoritarianism). The nation is bound by Catholic tradition, because its religion gives Belgium its civic cohesion and defines belonging (Religious Nationalism). The country keeps strong armed forces while refusing to take sides in foreign conflicts, since neutrality defends its sovereignty (Armed Neutrality). Rule by elected representatives and party bargaining is rejected because it breeds corruption and shuts the people's voice out (against Representative Democracy). Liberal individual rights and freedom of expression are rejected, since they erode the faith and the family (against Civil Liberalism). Revolutionary communism that abolishes the state and religion is rejected because it aims to destroy the church (against Communization). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected since duty to God sets the limit of conduct (against Amoralism). A reasoned worldview that grounds morality in human dignity and not revelation is rejected, because it is a way of leaving God out (against Secular Humanism).

Ba'athism.d: The Arab nation is one people split by borders, so that its scattered groups of one language and culture must be unified into a single state (Pan-Nationalism). The state owns the means of production and directs the economy centrally, because socialism ends exploitation and develops the nation's resources (State Socialism). A single party leads the state apparatus and the political process, since the vanguard of the nation should govern in place of rival representatives (Partocracy). Profits and resource rents of state-owned enterprises supply the main revenue for public spending, so that oil and industry serve the people (State Enterprise Revenue). Private markets free of government direction are rejected because they leave the nation's wealth to foreign and domestic exploiters (against Laissez-Faire). Rule by religious law and a deity's clergy is rejected, since the nation's identity is secular and Arab and not defined by one sect (against Theocracy).

Cosmist Vanguardism.d: Intelligence should expand without limit through energy capture, computation and space colonization, because life is meant to spread through the cosmos (Extropianism). The human body and mind are to be enhanced with cybernetics, genetic engineering and radical life extension, since a vanguard can overcome death by science (Transhumanism). Humanity should gain total mastery over nature and scarcity through automation and planned computation, so that labour is eradicated and abundance reaches all (Prometheanism).

Duginism.d: Social identity and geopolitical loyalty are anchored in great civilizational spheres, so that a continental Eurasian world stands as its own pole (Civilizationism). A single primordial tradition with a sacred metaphysical hierarchy is affirmed, because the ancient wisdom of the heartland holds an order the modern West has forgotten (Perennial Traditionalism). The heartland extends its dominance and influence over neighbouring territories, since a great power is measured by the space it commands (Imperialism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected because they make the world a single Atlantic market that dissolves peoples (against Globalism). A single human community with shared morality is rejected, since cosmopolitan universalism erases the distinct cultures of civilizations (against Cosmopolitanism). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because liberalism is the Western ideology that corrupts traditional societies (against Civil Liberalism). Free private transactions and commerce are rejected, since the sea power of merchants stands against the land power of the continent (against Laissez-Faire). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is rejected because multilateral order serves only the dominant unipolar power (against Internationalism). Disarmament and nonviolent settlement are rejected, since a civilization must be ready to fight for its sphere (against Pacifism).

Fiumanism.d: The state organizes industry into sectors in which workers' syndicates and employers cooperate, because every producer has a voice in a constitution drawn up by corporations of labour (Social-Corporatism). Society is grouped into corporate bodies of trades and professions by function, since the free city should rest on productive community and not on classes at war (Corporatism). The nation is an organic spirit with a heroic, poetic and mythic life, so that its destiny draws on legend and sacrifice (Romantic Nationalism).

Pekerism.d: A state-led push to build factories, power and infrastructure maximizes material abundance, because a poor country must industrialize through large-scale manufacturing (Industrialism). The state exerts directive influence over investment and plans key sectors rather than merely regulating them, since national development needs guidance (Dirigisme). One party leads the state apparatus and dominates the political process, so that national tasks are not delayed by competing representatives (Partocracy). Labour and employers are grouped in corporate bodies by function under state guidance, because the nation works as one body without class struggle (Corporatism). Rule by a deity's clergy and religious law is rejected since the republic's authority must be secular (against Theocracy). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because the personal liberties of liberalism may weaken the unity of the national project (against Civil Liberalism). Free private transactions without government intervention are rejected, since the economy must be built by the state (against Laissez-Faire).

Ethnonationalist Kemalism.d: The nation is defined by Turkish descent and ancestry, since shared ethnic kinship ties the people to its homeland (Ethnic Nationalism). A unitary state concentrates administrative authority in Ankara, because provinces are extensions that enforce one national order uniformly (Centralism). State-led industrial growth and large-scale manufacturing build national strength, so that material abundance serves independence (Industrialism). The state steers investment and key sectors with strong directive influence, since planned development needs central guidance (Dirigisme). Preventive policing, data collection and surveillance preserve domestic security, because crime and subversion must be stopped before they spread (Securitism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected since the state must stay secular (against Theocracy). A dictator or ruler who legitimizes power as defender of a religion is rejected because religious authority must not control politics (against Religious Authoritarianism). A single human community whose morality transcends nations is rejected, since loyalty belongs to the Turkish nation (against Cosmopolitanism). Recognizing and protecting coexisting communities with separate languages and autonomy is rejected, because it threatens national unity (against Multiculturalism). Splitting the territory into seceding sovereign units is rejected since the homeland is indivisible (against Patchwork).

Eneasism.d: The nation is defined by shared culture, language, traditions and heritage, because a people is held together by the legacy it passes on (Cultural Nationalism). Large-scale manufacturing, energy and infrastructure build material abundance, since a modern nation must develop its industry (Industrialism). The state exerts strong directive influence over investment and the market, so that national projects are planned and not left to chance (Dirigisme). The nation keeps a strong military to defend its sovereignty while refusing to take sides in conflicts, because armed neutrality protects independence (Armed Neutrality). Global free trade and open borders are rejected, since international interdependence undermines the nation's autonomy (against Globalism). A market without government intervention is rejected because private profit may put the national interest second (against Laissez-Faire).

Social Nationalism.d: The nation is a community of shared culture, language and traditions, since social solidarity grows from a common heritage (Cultural Nationalism). A market economy balanced with guarantees of social equity and universal solidarity insurance protects citizens, because competition needs a framework of fairness (Social Market). Tax rates that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that the strong carry more of the nation's common needs (Progressive Taxation). A single human community with a morality beyond national lines is rejected because duties to compatriots come before abstract humanity (against Cosmopolitanism). Free private transactions without regulation are rejected, since an unrestrained market abandons the weak members of the nation (against Laissez-Faire).

Ethnocacerismo.d: The nation is defined by indigenous ancestry and descent, because shared ethnic kinship ties the people to its homeland (Ethnic Nationalism). The army leads the state as its highest institution, since officers and reservists embody the nation's honour and order (Stratocracy). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, so that a common Andean tradition of sharing replaces private accumulation (Collective Distribution). Land is redistributed to the peasantry and farmed communally, because rural communities are the base of the people (Agrarian Socialism). Civilian life is mobilized through mandatory military service, since the reservist nation must be ready for national goals (Regimentalism). The nation is defined by a specific race and its pride, because the copper race holds the destiny of the country (Racial Nationalism). A free market without state intervention is rejected since it hands resources to foreign owners (against Laissez-Faire). Global free trade and open borders are rejected, because international integration dissolves the autonomy of the people (against Globalism). Opposing war and militarism is rejected since the people must keep arms for its defence (against Pacifism). Recognizing coexisting communities of other origins with equal autonomy is rejected, because the nation belongs to its original people (against Multiculturalism).

National Primitivism.d: Technological civilization, agriculture and the complex division of labour should be dismantled in favour of a return to wild life, because the nation's people lived free before industry (Primitivism). The nation is defined by ethnicity and shared descent within a homeland, since kinship ties the people to their land (Ethnic Nationalism). Primitive, organic tribal identities and ancient lineage bonds replace the modern state, so that the people returns to its kin and its local lineage (Tribalism). Large-scale manufacturing and extraction are rejected because industry destroys both the land and the people (against Industrialism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected, since international integration uproots peoples (against Globalism). A single human community beyond national or tribal loyalties is rejected because abstract humanity erases the roots of each people (against Cosmopolitanism). The recognition of coexisting communities within one territory is rejected since each people belongs on its own land (against Multiculturalism).

Social-Bonapartism.d: One strong ruler holds personal authority resting on the people, because a leader above parties can act for the whole nation (Autocracy). The state steers investment and key sectors through strong directive influence, since public works and credit for the working class need planning (Dirigisme). Railways, factories and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, so that industry gives the people work and prosperity (Industrialism). The state protects the health, housing and habits of citizens through guidance and welfare, because a paternal government secures their well-being (Civic Paternalism). Supreme authority is concentrated in the national government, which holds provinces as administrative divisions, since a unitary state enforces one order (Centralism). The nation extends its power and prestige over other territories through diplomacy and force, because glory abroad confirms the regime (Imperialism). Splitting the territory into seceding city-states is rejected since the national territory must stay united (against Patchwork).

Tridemism.d: Offices and rewards go to those with proven ability and merit, because a ruling order of talent serves everyone better than inherited rank or the crowd (Meritocracy). Land is taxed on its unimproved site value, so that the community recovers the rent from its natural resources (Land Value Tax). The state steers investment and key sectors with directive influence, since planned development needs central guidance (Dirigisme). Government looks after the welfare, habits and health of citizens through guidance, because a caring state forms responsible people (Civic Paternalism). Elected representatives who govern on behalf of citizens give the people a voice, since leaders must answer to those they serve (Representative Democracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship rather than ethnicity, so that belonging comes from commitment to the republic (Civic Nationalism). Rule driven by mass passions and the whim of the crowd is rejected because it hands power to those without judgement (against Ochlocracy).

Nationalist Kemalism.d: The state steers investment and industry with directive influence, because planned development secures the nation's strength (Dirigisme). Trades and professions are grouped in corporate bodies by function, since solidarism of classes replaces class conflict in the republic (Corporatism). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, so that the republic's order is kept from upheaval (Conservatism). Modern industry and science are embraced to strengthen the nation's heritage, because progress should serve the Turkish people and its past (Reactionary Modernism). One party dominates the state apparatus and the political process, since the party leads the nation toward its goals (Partocracy). The state is the ethical entity that unites individuals in a higher purpose, because the nation's will is realized through it (Ethical Statism). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, since Turkish identity gives the republic its soul (Cultural Nationalism). The nation is defined by ethnicity and shared descent, because the Turkish people's kinship ties it to its homeland (Ethnic Nationalism). Foreign policy pursues national interests through power and not through ideals, so that alliances serve the country's advantage (Realpolitik). The country stays out of foreign entanglements, because self-reliance protects independence (Isolationism). Factories, railways and heavy industry expand material abundance, since industrialization underpins sovereignty (Industrialism). Public etiquette and discipline are enforced in the national spirit, because order and decorum mark a civilized people (Disciplinarianism). Civilian life is mobilized through mandatory service and youth programmes, so that all citizens work for the nation (Regimentalism). Administrative authority is concentrated in Ankara, because a unitary state enforces one order in every province (Centralism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected since the state must remain secular and national (against Theocracy). Power shared between a central government and constituent states is rejected, because the republic is one and indivisible (against Federalism). Autonomous historical regions with their own parliaments are rejected since local identities may threaten unity (against Regionalism). A single human community beyond nations is rejected, because loyalty belongs to the Turkish nation (against Cosmopolitanism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process is rejected since individual rights must not weaken the national state (against Civil Libertarianism).

National Collectivism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because the nation's wealth is held in common for its people (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since solidarity of the people replaces the market (Collective Distribution). The state is the ethical whole that unites individuals in a higher purpose, so that private interest yields to the community (Ethical Statism). The nation is defined by ethnicity and shared descent, because the people's kinship is the basis of collective life (Ethnic Nationalism). Industry and science are embraced to strengthen the traditional nation, since modern power serves the people's inheritance (Reactionary Modernism). The country keeps apart from outside powers and trade, because self-reliance protects the collective (Isolationism). Ideas and doctrines are judged as tools for the nation's goals, so that whatever strengthens the collective counts as true (Instrumentalism). Factories and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, since heavy industry underpins independence (Industrialism). The state absorbs the individual, leaving no private sphere outside the collective, because personal life is subordinated to the common aim (Totalism). All decision-making is concentrated wholly in the capital, with uniformity suppressing regional difference, since one command runs the whole economy (Hypercentralism). Authority is concentrated in the national government, which treats districts as administrative units, because a unitary state applies one plan (Centralism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since private profit sets people against the collective (against Laissez-Faire). A single human community beyond nations is rejected, because the collective is the nation (against Cosmopolitanism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected since they weaken national self-sufficiency (against Globalism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process is rejected because rights of individuals must not obstruct the collective (against Civil Libertarianism). Consensual adult conduct without moral guidance is rejected, since the discipline of the collective shapes private life (against Permissivism).

Nazi-Maoism.d: Land is taken from landlords and given to the peasants, because the rural masses are the base of the movement (Agrarian Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since common provision supports the people's communes (Collective Distribution). Modern industry and science are embraced to strengthen the traditional race, so that technology serves ancestral heritage (Reactionary Modernism). One leader holds absolute power without restraint, because the helmsman embodies the will of the people (Autocracy). The state is the ethical whole that unites individuals in a higher purpose, since the movement's mission overrides private claims (Ethical Statism). The nation is defined by race and its purity, because the people's blood is the unit of struggle (Racial Nationalism). A different global order of fair exchange between nations is sought, since the poor lands must resist the powers that dominate them (Alter-Globalism). Ideas and doctrines are judged as tools for the revolution, so that whatever advances the struggle counts as true (Instrumentalism). Factories and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, because heavy industry is built alongside the countryside (Industrialism). The state absorbs the individual, leaving no private sphere outside the movement, since personal life is subordinated to the cause (Totalism). Civilian life is mobilized through mass campaigns and discipline, because every citizen serves the cause (Regimentalism). Authority is concentrated in the national government, which treats districts as administrative units, since a single centre commands the whole country (Centralism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private trade revives exploitation (against Laissez-Faire). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected, since personal freedom divides the movement (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives governing for rival parties are rejected because the movement speaks for the whole people (against Representative Democracy). Recognizing coexisting communities with separate customs is rejected, since a single people must hold the state (against Multiculturalism).

Savinkovism.d: The state steers investment and key industries with directive influence, because planned development under national leadership strengthens Russia (Dirigisme). Workers and employers are grouped in corporate bodies by function, since cooperation replaces class war (Corporatism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that wealth contributes to national tasks (Progressive Taxation). Modern industry and science are embraced to strengthen the nation's heritage, because technique serves the historic state (Reactionary Modernism). One leader holds absolute power without restraint, since a dictator can end the chaos of the revolution (Autocracy). The nation is a living spiritual community with its own soul and heroic past, so that Russia's destiny draws on its history (Romantic Nationalism). The country extends its power and dominance over other territories by force, because a great empire must hold its lands (Imperialism). Territories inhabited by compatriots under foreign rule are claimed for the homeland, since lost lands belong to the nation (Irredentism). Factories, railways and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, because industry gives the state power (Industrialism). Civilian life is mobilized through mandatory service and discipline, so that the whole people serves the state (Regimentalism). Authority is concentrated in the national government, which treats provinces as administrative divisions, because a unitary state enforces one order (Centralism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process is rejected, since individual rights would weaken the dictatorship (against Civil Libertarianism). Elected representatives governing on behalf of voters are rejected because assemblies of parties dissolve the state (against Representative Democracy). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is rejected, since Russia's interest must not be bound by joint commitments (against Internationalism). Disarmament and nonviolent settlement are rejected because force remains the instrument of the state (against Pacifism).

Mosleyism.d: Trades and professions are grouped in corporate bodies of employers and workers, because the corporate state ends class conflict and gives each industry self-government (Corporatism). Delegates are chosen through trade syndicates and professional guilds, so that producers take part in government through their occupations (Syndicracy). The state is the ethical whole that unites individuals in a higher purpose, since the nation's will lives in it (Ethical Statism). Modern industry and science are embraced to strengthen the nation's heritage, because technique and planning make Britain strong (Reactionary Modernism). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in a European civilization, since a united continent of nations could stand against rival blocs (Civilizationism). The country extends its power over other territories, because Africa and the Empire are to be developed by a great power (Imperialism). Tariffs and managed trade to build national wealth are favoured, since a closed economy of empire protects British workers (Mercantilism). Factories and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, because modern industry raises living standards (Industrialism). Civilian life is mobilized through drill and shared uniform, so that disciplined service binds citizens (Regimentalism). Authority is concentrated in the national government, which treats counties as administrative units, because a unitary state acts with decision (Centralism). Elected representatives governing for rival parties are rejected since the old gangs of Westminster are unable to act (against Representative Democracy). A market left free of regulation is rejected because unplanned competition causes unemployment (against Laissez-Faire). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process is rejected, since emergency must override individual claims (against Civil Libertarianism). A single human community beyond nations is rejected because loyalty comes first to Britain and its empire (against Cosmopolitanism). Disarmament and nonviolent settlement are rejected, since national strength rests on armed force (against Pacifism).

Revolutionary Nationalism.d: Workers organize in unions that take over the economy and its workplaces, because the nation's producers should run its industries (Syndicalism). Industries are run by worker guilds in a reciprocal relationship with a state, so that each craft governs its own work (Guild Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since the solidarity of the whole nation provides for every member (Collective Distribution). A path to modernity of its own, outside the dominant model, is followed because the nation breaks with the colonial past (Alternative Modernism). Delegates are chosen through trade syndicates, so that producers take part in government through their occupations (Syndicracy). Workers' councils of delegates run factories and neighbourhoods, since self-organization of working people is the base of the new nation (Councilism). All people who share the nation's language and origin should be united in one state across borders, because the divided homeland must be made whole (Pan-Nationalism). A different global order of fair exchange among nations is sought, since a free people must resist the dominant powers (Alter-Globalism). Matters are handled by the lowest competent authority, because decisions belong near the workers and villages (Subsidiarity). Town governance by popular assemblies keeps authority near the people, since the commune is the first form of national self-rule (Municipalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since international capital exploits the nation (against Laissez-Faire). Global free trade and open borders are rejected because they dissolve the nation's economy (against Globalism). Complete concentration of power in the capital is rejected, since it crushes the autonomy of workplaces and localities (against Hypercentralism). Concentrated authority in a national government is rejected because it replaces the producers' own organization (against Centralism).

Volkism.d: The nation is a living spiritual community with its own soul, folklore and heroic past, because the people finds its identity in myth and legend (Romantic Nationalism). The nation is defined by ethnicity and shared descent within a homeland, since kinship ties the people to its soil (Ethnic Nationalism). Farming and rural settlement are the foundation of society, so that the peasant rooted in the land keeps the people healthy (Agrarianism). A single leader embodies the people's will with absolute personal authority, because a folk needs one voice to act (Autocracy). A return to an earlier political order of the people is sought since modern developments are a decline from its roots (Reactionaryism). Large-scale manufacturing and city life are rejected because industry uproots the folk from its soil (against Industrialism). A single human community with a morality beyond peoples is rejected, since each folk has its own spirit that abstract humanity erases (against Cosmopolitanism). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because liberal freedom loosens the bonds that tie the folk together (against Civil Liberalism).

Optimateism.d: Power belongs to a distinguished class of inherited status and education, because those with a stake in the land and a long family tradition are best fitted to rule (Aristocracy). Inherited customs, natural obligations and ancestral order are preserved against rapid change, since institutions that have lasted hold a wisdom no reform can replace (Traditionalist Conservatism). Elected representatives who govern on behalf of voters are rejected because a general election makes leaders servants of popular favour (against Representative Democracy). Direct votes on laws through referendums are rejected, since the many cannot judge what the state requires (against Referendum Democracy). A tax whose rate falls as income rises is accepted because it leaves capital in the hands of those who bear responsibility for the commonwealth (Regressive Taxation). Rule driven by the mass of the poor and the passions of the crowd is rejected since it ends in plunder and demagogues (against Ochlocracy).

Integralism.d: Public and moral life is subordinated to revealed doctrine and the authority of the church, since the common good of society is a spiritual end that the state must serve (Religious Traditionalism). The ruler upholds religion and the faith against dissent, so that political power is guided by the church in matters of salvation (Religious Authoritarianism). A society is a community of mutual obligation and shared purpose, because the person is formed by family, parish and neighbourhood (Communitarianism). Powers rest with historical regions and local communities, since the capital cannot know each place's needs (Regionalism). Productive property is spread widely among families and small owners, so that no one depends wholly on employers or the state (Distributism). Trades and professions are grouped in guilds of employers and workers by function, because cooperation replaces class struggle (Corporatism). Property is shared among working households through guilds and cooperatives, since social justice requires that ownership be spread, as the church's teaching on the common good asks (Social-Distributism). Matters are handled by the lowest competent authority, because the higher body should only help what the family and the community cannot do (Subsidiarity). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected, since it makes personal choice the final judge against revealed truth (against Civil Liberalism). Free markets without moral limits are rejected because profit alone destroys families and just wages (against Laissez-Faire). Class-war revolution that abolishes private property is rejected since it denies God and the family (against Communization). State ownership by planners is rejected because it swallows the family and local bodies (against State Socialism). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected, since natural law binds every person (against Amoralism). A worldview that grounds ethics in human reason without revelation is rejected because it excludes God from public life (against Secular Humanism).

National Capitalism.d: The economy is free of government intervention and regulation, because private owners competing in open markets create the most wealth for the nation (Laissez-Faire). Revenue comes from duties on imports, so that tariffs fund the state and shield domestic producers from foreign competition (Tariff-Based Funding). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, since a market society needs a common tradition to hold it together (Cultural Nationalism). The country extends its power and influence over other territories by force and trade dominance, because national greatness opens markets (Imperialism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected because they let foreign interests undercut the country's own industry (against Globalism). A single human community beyond national lines is rejected, since the nation's citizens owe their duties to one another first (against Cosmopolitanism). State ownership with central planning is rejected because officials cannot match private owners in producing wealth (against State Socialism).

Carlism.d: Public life is subordinated to Catholic doctrine and church authority, since the traditional faith is the basis of the kingdom's laws (Religious Traditionalism). A monarch holds supreme authority unchecked by parliaments, because the legitimate king rules under God and the old laws (Absolute Monarchy). The nation is bound by the Catholic faith, so that religion gives Spain its identity and cohesion (Religious Nationalism). Historic regions keep their own laws and charters, since local rights older than the state protect each people (Regionalism). A union of sovereign regions formed by agreement ties the kingdom together, because provinces keep their own fueros under the crown (Confederalism). Trades and professions are grouped in corporate bodies of workers and employers, so that guilds express social life by function (Corporatism). The law should enforce traditional morality through the state, because public virtue protects the common good (Legal Moralism). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected, since liberal freedom dissolves the faith and the old order (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who govern in the name of the people are rejected because parliaments usurp the king's legitimate power (against Representative Democracy). A unitary state that concentrates administration in the capital is rejected, since it crushes the historic rights of regions (against Centralism). Free private markets without moral limits are rejected because they break traditional guilds and village life (against Laissez-Faire). Class-war revolution is rejected since it is atheist and abolishes the family and property (against Communization). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected because the divine law binds all (against Amoralism). A reasoned worldview without revelation is rejected, since it removes the faith from the state (against Secular Humanism).

Autocratic Monarchism.d: A hereditary monarch holds supreme power without limit, because divinely sanctioned succession gives one sovereign the right to rule the state (Absolute Monarchy). The ruler exercises absolute authority without external legal restraints, since a single will can decide where councils cannot (Autocracy). Elected representatives who govern on behalf of voters are rejected because parliamentary rule divides the realm into factions (against Representative Democracy). A crown whose powers are limited by a constitution is rejected, since a sovereign bound by a charter is no longer the source of law (against Constitutional Monarchy). The crown passes by inheritance within a dynasty surrounded by a nobility and a court, and the sovereign rules by divine right and personal decree over the realm. A single strong leader holds absolute power over the countryside, because village life needs decisive personal command. Rule by elected representatives and party politics is rejected since parties divide the nation. A hereditary monarch holds supreme authority beside the people's councils, because the tsar embodies the nation's unity above classes. Rule by elected representatives is rejected because ranks and oaths, not votes, give authority. Elected representatives who govern on behalf of voters are rejected because a general election makes leaders servants of popular favour. One leader holds absolute power without restraint, because the helmsman embodies the will of the people. One ruler holds personal power without effective restraint, since a strong president alone can guarantee stability. Elected representatives who legislate on behalf of voters are rejected because city parties do not speak for the farming people. A monarch holds supreme authority without limit, so that the throne is the sacred source of law. Inherited customs, the Orthodox church and natural obligations are preserved, because traditional values protect the nation from decadent influence. A monarch holds supreme authority unchecked by parliaments, because the legitimate king rules under God and the old laws. Elected representatives governing for rival parties are rejected since the old gangs of Westminster are unable to act. One leader holds unrestrained power over the state, because firm command can keep a free economy and social order together.

Theocratic Distributism.d: Government is ruled by religious clergy and divine law, because the community's highest authority is a deity whose commands order the state (Theocracy). Productive property is spread widely among families and small owners, so that every household holds land or a trade of its own (Distributism). Public life is subordinated to revealed doctrine and tradition, since the sacred law defines what is just (Religious Traditionalism). A society is a community of mutual obligation, because families and congregations share duties rather than competing as individuals (Communitarianism). A market without moral limits or sharing is rejected since concentrated wealth and usury dissolve the community (against Laissez-Faire). State ownership by planners is rejected because it replaces the household's own property with officials (against State Socialism). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected, since divine law sets the bounds of conduct (against Amoralism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason without revelation is rejected because it drives God out of the common order (against Secular Humanism).

Reactionary Feudalism.d: A society of lords, vassals and personal loyalty tied to land gives each person a fixed place, because the medieval order protected its people through bonds of service (Feudalism). A return to a previous political state of society is sought, since the modern order is a decline from an older and better one (Reactionaryism). Power belongs to a landed ruling class of inherited status, so that the best families guard the realm through duty (Aristocracy). Belief in advance through reform is rejected because change only dissolves old bonds and loyalties (against Progressivism). Rule by elected representatives of equal voters is rejected, since it breaks the chain of obligation between lord and vassal (against Representative Democracy). A tax whose rate falls as income rises is accepted since the landed bear the burden of protection and the lower ranks owe their dues (Regressive Taxation). Rule by the passions of the common crowd is rejected because it overthrows the natural order of ranks (against Ochlocracy).

Neo-Absolutism.d: A single sovereign holds undivided power over the state, because divided authority invites faction while an absolute monarch can govern with efficiency (Absolute Monarchy). A reactionary critique treats democracy as a failed experiment, so that the state should be run like a firm by a sovereign who owns it (Neoreactionaryism). Elected representatives who govern for voters are rejected since competing parties turn politics into a struggle for spoils (against Representative Democracy). Direct votes on laws through referendums are rejected because popular majorities cannot administer a state (against Referendum Democracy). The belief that societies advance through reform is rejected, since progress in democratic politics has produced decline (against Progressivism).

Aristocratic Cameralism.d: The state is managed like a great estate through professional administration, because trained officials advance the treasury and the prosperity of the realm (Cameralism). Power belongs to a distinguished class of inherited rank and education, since an aristocracy is bred for service to the crown (Aristocracy). A return to a previous political order is sought, so that old institutions govern the economy again (Reactionaryism). The state owns and runs major enterprises while keeping a market economy, because royal workshops and monopolies fill the public purse (State Capitalism). Elected representatives who govern on behalf of voters are rejected since officials and nobles, not parties, should rule (against Representative Democracy). Rule driven by mass passions is rejected because the unlearned crowd cannot manage the state's finances (against Ochlocracy).

Feudal Monarchism.d: A society of lords, vassals and personal loyalty bound by land holds the realm together, because duties flow from oaths between persons and not from a distant bureaucracy (Feudalism). Inherited customs and natural obligations are preserved since institutions of the past carry accumulated wisdom (Traditionalist Conservatism). Power belongs to a landed ruling class of inherited status, so that noble houses stand between the king and the people (Aristocracy). Rule by elected representatives is rejected because ranks and oaths, not votes, give authority (against Representative Democracy). Belief in advance through reform is rejected since change breaks the bonds of homage (against Progressivism). A king's overlordship over vassal rulers who keep internal self-rule gives the realm its structure, because the crown commands them in war and foreign affairs while they manage their own land (Suzerainty).

Clerical Monarchism.d: A king rules as the defender of the faith, so that religious legitimacy crushes dissent and unifies the throne with the church (Religious Authoritarianism). Public life is subordinated to church doctrine, since the throne rests on revealed tradition (Religious Traditionalism). The nation is bound by the religion of its people, because the crown and altar give the kingdom its identity (Religious Nationalism). A monarch holds supreme authority without limit, so that the throne is the sacred source of law (Absolute Monarchy). A monarchy with a limited parliament under a charter is accepted as a compromise, because the king still appoints ministers and keeps strong prerogatives (Semi-Constitutional Monarchy). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected since freedom of conscience undermines the throne and altar (against Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives who govern for voters are rejected because parliaments challenge the crown and the church (against Representative Democracy). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected, since moral law comes from God (against Amoralism). A reasoned worldview without revelation is rejected because it removes the church from public life (against Secular Humanism).

Developmental Theocracy.d: Government is ruled by clergy and divine law, because the deity's commands order the state and its modernization (Theocracy). The nation is bound by its religion, so that faith gives citizens cohesion in building the country (Religious Nationalism). Large-scale manufacturing and infrastructure expand material abundance, since an industrial base is needed for the strength of the faithful (Industrialism). Inherited customs and religious obligations are preserved while the economy advances, because tradition holds society together amid rapid change (Traditionalist Conservatism). The state steers investment and key sectors with strong directive influence, since religious authority plans the national economy (Dirigisme). Public life is subordinated to revealed doctrine, so that development stays inside the bounds of scripture (Religious Traditionalism). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected because divine law limits what progress may do (against Amoralism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason without revelation is rejected since development must serve the faith (against Secular Humanism).

Classical Eurasianism.d: Social identity and loyalty are anchored in great civilizational spheres, because the Eurasian steppe and its peoples form a distinct world of their own (Civilizationism). Inherited customs and religious bonds are preserved against rapid modernization, since the Orthodox and steppe heritage guards the peoples of the continent (Traditionalist Conservatism). Foreign policy pursues the state's interests through power and not moral ideals, so that the continental heartland defends its position by cold calculation (Realpolitik).
