The state exerts directive influence over investment and key sectors, because planned development protects the heartland's autonomy (Dirigisme). Global free trade and open borders are rejected since the Atlantic order would dissolve the continent's own economic space (against Globalism). The protection of individual rights and expression is rejected because Western liberal ideals do not fit Eurasian peoples (against Civil Liberalism). A leading state's overlordship over the peripheral territories that keep their internal self-rule gives the continent its order, since the centre holds their foreign affairs and defence (Suzerainty).

Mladorossism.d: A hereditary monarch holds supreme authority beside the people's councils, because the tsar embodies the nation's unity above classes (Absolute Monarchy). The state owns and plans production in the interest of the whole people, so that the economy is run for labour and not private profit (State Socialism). Public life rests on the Orthodox tradition, since the church gives the realm its moral order (Religious Traditionalism). Civilian life is mobilized through mandatory service and youth discipline, because the nation's young are raised for common tasks (Regimentalism). The state steers investment and key sectors with directive influence, since planning produces development (Dirigisme). A market free of government intervention is rejected because private profit sets the owner above the people (against Laissez-Faire). Rule by elected representatives and party politics is rejected since parties divide the nation (against Representative Democracy).

National Social Capitalism.d: A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and universal solidarity insurance, because the nation's capitalism should protect its workers (Social Market). Tax rates rise with income so that higher incomes carry more of the burden, since solidarity within the nation requires shared sacrifice (Progressive Taxation). The nation is defined by ethnicity and shared descent, so that the people with a common origin forms the community of solidarity (Ethnic Nationalism). Administrative power is concentrated in the national government, because a unitary state ensures the same social protections everywhere (Centralism). Recognizing coexisting communities with separate customs and languages is rejected since the welfare of the nation rests on a single people (against Multiculturalism).

Right-State Liberalism.d: A market economy without government intervention is the best path, because voluntary exchange among owners produces prosperity (Laissez-Faire). A single flat tax rate applied to all income is fair, since equal treatment under the tax code avoids punishing earnings (Flat Taxation). The protection of individual rights and expression against any authority is a core aim, so that each person is free to live as they choose (Civil Liberalism). Revenue from state-owned enterprises is rejected because government should not run businesses that private owners can run (against State Enterprise Revenue). A single flat tax rate applied to all income is fair, since equal rates respect every earner.

Monarquia Syndicalista.d: Workers' unions manage production and organize each trade, because syndicates of producers give labour an honourable place under the crown (Syndicalism). Public life is shaped by the Catholic church's teaching, since tradition and the faith ground the moral order of the kingdom (Religious Traditionalism). A monarch rules with a limited parliament under a charter but keeps strong prerogatives, because the crown stands above parties as guardian of the nation (Semi-Constitutional Monarchy). Delegates are chosen through trade syndicates and professional guilds, so that producers represent their occupations in the cortes (Syndicracy). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, since Portugal's history gives the monarchy its legitimacy (Cultural Nationalism). The country avoids alliances and wars abroad, because neutrality keeps the nation safe (Non-Interventionism). Public etiquette and order are enforced, so that decorum and discipline mark a civilized people (Disciplinarianism). Autonomous historical regions with their own councils are recognized, because the provinces keep their own rights under the crown (Regionalism). Matters are handled by the lowest competent authority, since higher bodies should only help what municipalities and guilds cannot do (Subsidiarity). A market left free of regulation is rejected because unrestrained profit divides the realm (against Laissez-Faire). Elected representatives governing for rival parties are rejected since party rule divides the people and weakens the throne (against Representative Democracy). One ruler with absolute power is rejected, because the crown is bound by law and by the guilds (against Autocracy). Complete concentration of power in the capital is rejected since the realm rests on local bodies and trades (against Hypercentralism).

Serenissimism.d: The state is managed like a great estate through professional administration, because the Republic's offices treat public finance as a trust of the city (Cameralism). Merchants and craftsmen are grouped in corporate bodies, since guilds and scuole give each trade its place (Corporatism). Revenue comes from duties on imports and shipping, so that customs on trade fund the fleet and arsenal (Tariff-Based Funding). Inherited customs and natural obligations are preserved against rapid change, because a long tradition of the Republic holds wisdom (Traditionalist Conservatism). Power belongs to patrician families of inherited status, since the noble houses are bred to serve the city (Aristocracy). A small elite governs, so that a closed council of merchants and nobles rules for the common good (Oligarchy). Society is a community of mutual obligation, because citizens belong to parishes and confraternities (Communitarianism). Tariffs and managed trade to build national wealth are favoured, since the state directs commerce for its own interest (Mercantilism). The law may enforce traditional morality, so that public virtue sustains the Republic (Legal Moralism). A ruler's overlordship over subject cities that keep local self-rule gives the maritime state its reach, because the capital holds their defence and foreign affairs (Suzerainty). Direct votes on laws through referendums are rejected, since the mass of the people cannot decide matters of state (against Referendum Democracy). A revolution abolishing classes and property is rejected because it would destroy the order of the Republic (against Communization). An economy free of state direction is rejected, since commerce is a public concern under magistrates (against Laissez-Faire). A single human community beyond cities is rejected because loyalty belongs to the Republic of St Mark (against Cosmopolitanism).

National Conservatism.d: The nation is defined by shared culture, language and heritage, because a people's inherited traditions give its institutions their roots (Cultural Nationalism). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, since accumulated customs hold a wisdom that reformers lack (Conservatism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that accountable lawmakers keep the nation's consent under its constitution (Representative Democracy). The law may enforce traditional moral standards, because shared public morality sustains the national community (Legal Moralism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected since international integration weakens the self-government of nations (against Globalism). A single human community beyond national lines is rejected because duties to fellow citizens come before abstract humanity (against Cosmopolitanism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is rejected, since supranational institutions override national sovereignty (against Internationalism). Sovereignty, secure borders, controlled immigration and a constitutional parliament protect the nation's self-government and its customs. Established institutions and gradual change are preferred, since the working class prefers the family, the union hall and the local church to experiments. Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because a labour party seeks the votes of ordinary people in free elections. Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a constitutional republic gives consent its place. Established institutions, family and gradual change are preferred, since faith-based associations and local communities strengthen people better than distant bureaucracies.

Paternalistic Conservatism.d: Business is run with a duty of care toward employees and the community, because owners have obligations to those who depend on them (Paternalistic Capitalism). The state protects the health, habits and living conditions of citizens through guidance and welfare, since the established order must care for the weak (Civic Paternalism). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, so that society keeps its customs while it relieves hardship (Conservatism). The nation is held together by shared culture and heritage, because the duties of rank bind high and low in one people (Cultural Nationalism). Tax rates that rise as income rises shift the burden toward higher incomes, since privilege carries obligations to the poor (Progressive Taxation). An economy free of government intervention and regulation is rejected because private transactions for profit neglect the duties of the wealthy (against Laissez-Faire).

Buchanan Paleoconservatism.d: Authentic conservatism defends the nation's inherited faith, family and sovereignty over utopian reform, because the republic was built by a specific people with its own traditions (Paleoconservatism). The nation is a culture with a common language and heritage, since American identity is carried by the settled people and not by an abstract creed (Cultural Nationalism). Tariffs on imports fund the government and shield workers, so that factories and wages stay at home (Tariff-Based Funding). The country minds its own affairs and stays out of foreign entanglements, because America first means keeping its sons out of distant wars (Isolationism). Law may uphold the moral order of the community, since a culture war is won when public standards defend the family (Legal Moralism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected because they sacrifice jobs and sovereignty to multinational interests (against Globalism). Military interference in the affairs of other countries is rejected, since empire abroad costs blood and treasure without securing the homeland (against Interventionism). A single human community beyond national lines is rejected because loyalty belongs to fellow citizens and not to a borderless world (against Cosmopolitanism).

Hard Right Paleoconservatism.d: Authentic conservatism guards the settled customs, order and religion of a historic people, because a durable civilization depends on authority and hierarchy rather than on experiments in equality (Paleoconservatism). The nation is defined by shared culture, language, traditions and heritage, since a common inheritance binds its citizens against fragmentation (Cultural Nationalism). The country avoids entanglement with foreign powers and keeps to its own borders, so that its strength is spent on domestic order (Isolationism). The law enforces traditional morality against vice and disorder, because public decency is a precondition for a stable community (Legal Moralism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected since international integration dissolves national identity and authority (against Globalism). Military intervention in other countries' affairs is rejected because crusades abroad strain the country's own order (against Interventionism). Faith in improvement through reform and the equality agenda is rejected, since movements for progress erode the old hierarchies that keep society steady (against Progressivism).

Old Right Paleoconservatism.d: Authentic conservatism defends the faith, family and the nation's inherited traditions against the state, because the founders' republic was a modest and decentralized one (Paleoconservatism). The nation is a community of shared heritage, language and customs, since citizens are bound by a particular patrimony and not by ideology (Cultural Nationalism). The country keeps out of foreign alliances and quarrels, so that its government stays small and its liberties intact (Isolationism). Sovereignty is shared between a federal government and constituent states, since each state keeps its own authority and the federal level has limited enumerated powers (Federalism). Military intervention in the affairs of other countries is rejected because war and empire enlarge the state at home (against Interventionism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected since supranational integration erodes the self-government of the republic (against Globalism).

Neoconservatism.d: Democratic states should use their power to shape other countries, because security and freedom are protected by acting abroad with force and diplomacy (Interventionism). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, since the American creed, not ancestry, gives everyone a place (Civic Nationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that accountable government and the spread of democracy are the foundation of legitimacy (Representative Democracy). Government provides only a basic safety net for the poor, because welfare beyond that breeds dependency and weakens character (Residualism). Market institutions and established order are defended with moral seriousness, since conservative values give liberal society its footing (Liberal Conservatism). Withdrawing from world affairs is rejected because retreat invites aggression and tyranny (against Isolationism). Staying out of foreign conflicts and alliances is rejected, since passivity lets rivals shape the global order (against Non-Interventionism).

Mesoconservatism.d: Prudent change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, because a moderate path keeps what works while avoiding both extremes and stagnation (Conservatism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since pragmatic coalitions of parliament hold the centre together (Representative Democracy). Active engagement in other countries' affairs is accepted when national interests require it, so that the country shapes outcomes abroad with measured force (Interventionism). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship rather than ethnicity, because a common civic loyalty unites a plural public (Civic Nationalism).

Red Toryism.d: Inherited customs, natural obligations and the wisdom of old institutions are preserved, because a settled community should not be uprooted by the market or the state (Traditionalist Conservatism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since neighbours, churches and local associations give people belonging (Communitarianism). The crown is a ceremonial head of state under the law, so that continuity and a shared past stand above party (Constitutional Monarchy). The nation is held together by shared culture and heritage, because a common story binds the commons to the country (Cultural Nationalism). Property is spread widely among households and local owners, since a society of small proprietors, co-operatives and mutual guilds gives working families independence (Social-Distributism). Business is run with a duty of care toward employees and the community, because owners hold obligations that go beyond profit (Paternalistic Capitalism). A market free of regulation is rejected since unrestrained trade hollows out local shops, towns and old bonds (against Laissez-Faire).

Green Conservatism.d: Nature and wild ecosystems have intrinsic value and deserve protection, because the countryside and its landscapes are a trust to be handed on (Conservationism). Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation and renewable energy is needed, since a prudent society cannot spend its natural capital (Environmentalism). Prudent change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, so that the stewardship of land belongs to conserving what generations have built (Conservatism). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and universal solidarity insurance, because a steady economy needs both enterprise and care for the common good (Social Market).

Clerical Conservatism.d: Public life is subordinated to revealed doctrine and the church's moral teaching, because religious tradition is the oldest guide to the good of society (Religious Traditionalism). The nation is bound by the faith of its people, since shared worship gives its culture its identity and cohesion (Religious Nationalism). The law may enforce traditional morality, so that public standards uphold the dignity of marriage, family and life (Legal Moralism). Consensual adult conduct without moral guidance is not left alone, because licence loosens the bonds that sustain a believing community (against Permissivism). Belief in advance through reform that revises the faith is rejected, since the established teaching should not bend to fashion (against Progressivism). An ethic of desire without commandments is rejected because the moral law has a divine author (against Amoralism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason without revelation is rejected, since it excludes the church from public life (against Secular Humanism).

Gaullism.d: The state steers investment and key industries with strong directive influence, because national independence needs a planned economy led by the state (Dirigisme). Authority is concentrated in the national government and administered from Paris, since a unitary state with strong executive guarantees national unity (Centralism). The nation is a historic community of shared culture and language, so that a certain idea of France gives its people grandeur (Cultural Nationalism). The country keeps its own strong military and nuclear deterrent while refusing blocs, because independence from superpowers needs armed neutrality (Armed Neutrality). The state looks after the welfare and habits of citizens through guidance and social programmes, since the leader guards the people's well-being (Civic Paternalism).

Free-Market Conservatism.d: An economy left free of state intervention produces wealth and liberty, because private property and competition reward effort and discover prices (Laissez-Faire). Established institutions, family and gradual change are preserved, since market order depends on a moral framework inherited from the past (Conservatism). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, so that every citizen who accepts the constitution belongs (Civic Nationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because accountable legislatures limit power and protect property (Representative Democracy). State ownership and central planning are rejected since officials cannot match the knowledge held by market participants (against State Socialism). Tax rates that climb with income are rejected because penalizing success discourages saving and investment (against Progressive Taxation). Revenue from state-owned enterprises is rejected, since government should not run businesses that private firms can manage (against State Enterprise Revenue). Workplaces run through councils of workers and consumers are rejected because collective planning replaces choice and profit with committees (against Participatory Economics).

Agrarian Conservatism.d: Farming and rural settlement are the foundation of a healthy society, because working the soil forms self-reliant families rooted in a place (Agrarianism). Productive property, especially land, is spread among many households, since widespread ownership keeps people independent of banks and big business (Distributism). Established customs and gradual change are preferred, so that the village and the farm carry accumulated wisdom (Conservatism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, because neighbours depend on one another in the seasons of planting and harvest (Communitarianism). Large-scale manufacturing and urban extraction are rejected since factories draw people from the land and weaken rural life (against Industrialism). Smallholders, family farms, village cooperatives and neighbourly mutual help keep the countryside self-reliant, in a modest local economy where property is widely held and tradition is respected. Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, because social protection should be built on family, community and tradition rather than on rupture.

Liberal Toryism.d: Pragmatic reform within the tradition is accepted, because a conservative party can protect national institutions by adapting them to social needs (Progressive Conservatism). Free trade and open borders on a global basis expand prosperity, since international integration benefits an outward-looking country (Globalism). Prudent change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, so that liberal measures serve to conserve order (Conservatism).

Social Gaullism.d: Workers share in the profits and decisions of the firms that employ them through participation schemes, because association of capital and labour ends class strife and binds the worker to the nation (Yellow Socialism). The state looks after the welfare and habits of citizens through guidance and social programmes, since a caring leadership secures their dignity (Civic Paternalism). The country keeps its own strong military while refusing blocs, because independence needs armed neutrality (Armed Neutrality). Pragmatic reform within the tradition is accepted, since a conservative movement can advance social measures to keep the nation united (Progressive Conservatism). A market in which firms and banks coordinate with workers and long-term cooperation is favoured, so that the economy balances social partners rather than short-term profit (Rhine Capitalism).

Neo-Gaullism.d: The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, because the republic is open to all who adhere to its ideals of French grandeur (Civic Nationalism). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government in Paris, since a unified state guarantees the equality of all citizens (Centralism). Enterprise and market institutions are respected together with the nation's established order, so that a liberal conservative right modernizes the economy while keeping its traditions (Liberal Conservatism). The republic is a project of independence and grandeur, and its leaders are expected to serve the country above party and to keep France in command of its own destiny.

Bonapartist Gaullism.d: A strong president holds personal authority above parties, because the leader's direct bond with the people lets him decide for the nation (Autocracy). All authority is concentrated in the capital, which suppresses regional autonomy, since one uniform administration serves the state's grandeur (Hypercentralism). The state steers investment and key industries with strong directive influence, so that the economy is planned for independence (Dirigisme). Large-scale manufacturing, nuclear power and infrastructure expand material abundance, because industrial strength underpins national standing (Industrialism). The country keeps its own strong military and refuses alignment with blocs, since armed neutrality protects independence from the superpowers (Armed Neutrality). The nation is a historic community of shared culture and language, so that its glory and greatness shape its public life (Cultural Nationalism).

Conservative Atlanticism.d: Social identity and loyalty are anchored in a Western civilization, because the transatlantic community shares heritage and security interests against rival blocs (Civilizationism). Foreign policy pursues the state's interests through power rather than moral ideals, since stability among allies matters more than crusades (Realpolitik). Market institutions and established order are respected, so that a free economy and cautious conservatism go hand in hand (Liberal Conservatism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because accountable democracy distinguishes the Western alliance from autocracies (Representative Democracy).

Neoconservative Atlanticism.d: Democratic states use their power in other countries when needed, because the Western alliance defends order and freedom through force and diplomacy (Interventionism). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in a transatlantic civilization, since its values bind allies together against authoritarian rivals (Civilizationism). Preventive policing, intelligence and surveillance preserve security, because terrorism and subversion must be stopped before they strike (Securitism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that democracy at home is a model to spread among allies (Representative Democracy).

One-Nation Conservatism.d: The state looks after the welfare and living conditions of all classes through guidance and social provision, because those with privilege owe a duty to the poor and the nation stays united (Civic Paternalism). Pragmatic reform within the tradition is accepted, since a conservative party must adapt the order to keep the loyalty of working people (Progressive Conservatism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that the better-off carry the cost of cohesion (Progressive Taxation). A market free of regulation is rejected because unchecked competition splits the country into two nations of rich and poor (against Laissez-Faire). A revolution that abolishes classes and private property is rejected, since social peace depends on bonds between ranks rather than on conflict (against Communization).

Conservative Kemalism.d: Administrative authority is concentrated in Ankara, because a unitary state keeps the republic's reforms enforced evenly across provinces (Centralism). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and the republic's heritage, since a Turkish identity gives citizens cohesion (Cultural Nationalism). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, so that the republic's order is guarded from upheaval (Conservatism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because the state must stay secular and its laws made by the nation (against Theocracy).

Conservative Technoliberalism.d: Economy and daily life move beyond manufacturing toward knowledge, services and information, because digital and scientific work create the new wealth (Post-Industrialism). Global free trade and open borders benefit the connected economy, since cross-border data, talent and capital flow to those who open their markets (Globalism). Safeguarding personal privacy, speech and due process against state power is essential, so that innovation and enterprise stay free (Civil Libertarianism). Market institutions and established order are respected, because a stable framework of property and rules lets technology thrive (Liberal Conservatism).

Right-Social Authoritarianism.d: Preventive policing, data collection and surveillance preserve domestic security, because disorder and crime must be stopped before they grow (Securitism). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government, since a unitary state enforces one standard of order (Centralism). One strong leader holds personal authority above rivals, so that decisive command can keep society safe and stable (Autocracy). Established institutions and gradual change are preferred, because order depends on conserving what already works (Conservatism). The state looks after the health, habits and welfare of citizens through guidance and benefits, since care for the people secures their loyalty (Civic Paternalism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process against the state is rejected because liberty claims obstruct security (against Civil Libertarianism).

Kjærsgaardism.d: The nation is a community of shared language, customs and heritage, because Danish culture and its welfare society must be defended by those who inherit it (Cultural Nationalism). The belief in one human community with a morality that transcends nations is rejected, since solidarity works only among fellow citizens who share trust and duties (against Cosmopolitanism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected because they bring mass migration and international bodies that overrule the people's own decisions (against Globalism).

Kekkonism.d: The country keeps a credible defence while refusing to join blocs, because neutrality towards the great powers protects a small state's independence (Armed Neutrality). Wage and economic policy is negotiated among the state, employers and trade unions in permanent tripartite bodies, since social partnership keeps industrial peace (Neocorporatism). Forestry, factories and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, so that export industry sustains the nation (Industrialism). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government in the capital, because a strong presidency must steer the whole country (Centralism). The state exerts strong directive influence over investment and key sectors, since planned development guards economic independence (Dirigisme).

Reform Gaullism.d: Wages and policy are negotiated among the state, employers and unions in standing tripartite bodies, because social partnership by agreement reduces conflict (Neocorporatism). Pragmatic reform within the tradition is accepted, since a conservative movement should modernize institutions to preserve national cohesion (Progressive Conservatism). Workers share in profits and decisions of firms through participation schemes, so that capital and labour are associated and class strife fades (Yellow Socialism).

Paleoconservatism.d: Authentic conservatism defends faith, family, inherited custom and local community against the managerial state, because a nation grows from its own history and not from abstract theory (Paleoconservatism). The nation is defined by shared culture, language and heritage, since a people's patrimony binds it together (Cultural Nationalism). Productive property is spread among many households, so that wide ownership of land and shops keeps families independent (Distributism). Duties on imports fund the government and protect domestic industry, because tariffs favour the national worker (Tariff-Based Funding). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a constitutional republic gives consent its place (Representative Democracy). The law may enforce traditional morality, because public standards sustain the common life (Legal Moralism). The country minds its own affairs and avoids foreign entanglements, so that the republic is not turned into an empire (Isolationism). Power is divided between the federal and state governments, since limited union preserves local self-rule (Federalism). Military intervention in other countries is rejected because it costs the nation's sons and liberties (against Interventionism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected, since they dissolve national cohesion and workers' wages (against Globalism). A single human community beyond nations is rejected because loyalties are owed first to the home and the country (against Cosmopolitanism). Recognizing coexisting communities as equals with separate customs is rejected since a nation needs a shared way of life (against Multiculturalism).

Putinism.d: The state owns and runs major enterprises within a market economy, because strategic companies in energy and defence must serve the sovereign (State Capitalism). Corporations hold effective political power through close ties with the government, since loyal business magnates run key sectors (Corporatocracy). The state steers investment and key sectors with strong directive influence, so that planned development rebuilds national power (Dirigisme). A single flat tax rate applied to all income is fair, because a uniform rate is simple and hard to evade (Flat Taxation). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred since order follows the chaos of the 1990s (Conservatism). Inherited customs, the Orthodox church and natural obligations are preserved, because traditional values protect the nation from decadent influence (Traditionalist Conservatism). One ruler holds personal power without effective restraint, since a strong president alone can guarantee stability (Autocracy). A small elite of associates governs for its own gain, because proximity to the leader decides wealth and office (Oligarchy). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in a Russian civilization with its own path, since the Russian world differs from the West (Civilizationism). The country extends its power and influence over neighbouring territories, because a great power has a sphere around it (Imperialism). Foreign policy pursues national interests through power and not through ideals, so that deals follow strength (Realpolitik). Territories inhabited by compatriots under foreign rule are claimed for the homeland, since protecting Russians abroad justifies action (Irredentism). Large-scale industry, pipelines and defence manufacturing expand material abundance, because heavy industry underpins sovereignty (Industrialism). Ideas and doctrines are judged as tools of the state, so that whatever serves the interest of the regime counts as useful (Instrumentalism). Preventive policing, data collection and surveillance preserve order, because security services must stop opposition early (Securitism). Administrative authority is concentrated in Moscow, since a vertical of power makes regions executors of the centre (Centralism). A single human community beyond nations is rejected because loyalty belongs to the Russian state (against Cosmopolitanism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process is rejected, since individual rights must not weaken the state (against Civil Libertarianism).

Post-Soviet Autocracy.d: The state owns and runs major enterprises within a market economy, because the ruling group controls strategic firms and banks (State Capitalism). Corporations hold effective political power through ties to the ruler, since business and government are fused (Corporatocracy). A single flat tax rate applied to all income is fair, so that a simple rate attracts investment and shields insiders (Flat Taxation). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, because stability comes before reform (Conservatism). One ruler holds personal power without effective restraint, since elections only confirm the incumbent (Autocracy). A small elite of insiders governs for its own gain, because patronage networks divide the state's wealth (Oligarchy). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values rather than ethnicity, since all who live in the republic are called its people (Civic Nationalism). Foreign policy pursues national interests through power and not through ideals, so that the ruler bargains with any partner (Realpolitik). Factories, mines and extraction expand material abundance, because raw-material industry funds the regime (Industrialism). Preventive policing, data collection and surveillance preserve order, since security agencies keep rivals under watch (Securitism). Administrative authority is concentrated in the capital, because appointed governors keep regions in line (Centralism). Safeguarding privacy, speech and due process is rejected, since civil rights threaten the incumbent (against Civil Libertarianism). Power shared between the central government and constituent states is rejected because regional authority is a threat to the vertical (against Federalism). Direct votes on laws through referendums are rejected, since popular votes outside the ruler's control are dangerous (against Referendum Democracy).

Radicalism.d: The protection of individual rights and expression, including freedom of conscience and the press, is the first purpose of politics, because citizens are equal under law (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since assemblies chosen by the people hold power accountable (Representative Democracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, so that every citizen of the republic belongs by loyalty to its principles (Civic Nationalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions serves peace, because the republic's ideals reach beyond borders (Internationalism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason and human dignity, without revelation, guides public life (Secular Humanism). Citizens chosen by lot form assemblies that decide public questions, since random selection gives ordinary people a share of political power (Demarchy). Rule by religious clergy and divine law is rejected because the state belongs to the people and not to a church (against Theocracy). A ruler who legitimizes power as a defender of a religion is rejected, since faith must not command the republic (against Religious Authoritarianism). A hereditary sovereign with unlimited power is rejected because every public office must be open to merit and election (against Absolute Monarchy).

Third Way.d: A politics beyond old left and right combines market dynamism with social investment, because modern government should enable people to work, learn and compete rather than only redistribute (Third Way). The economy shifts from manufacturing toward knowledge, services and information, since digital skills and education create the new wealth (Post-Industrialism). The protection of individual rights and expression is upheld along with equal opportunity, so that every person can shape their own life (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because accountable pragmatic government drives reform through parliaments (Representative Democracy). Global free trade and open borders expand prosperity, since interdependence rewards countries that open their markets and adapt (Globalism).

Christian Democracy.d: A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and universal solidarity insurance, because the dignity of the person calls for both enterprise and protection of families (Social Market). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a constitutional democracy built by Christian parties respects pluralism and consent (Representative Democracy). Public life draws on revealed doctrine and the moral teaching of the church, so that tradition and conscience guide policy (Religious Traditionalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is favoured because reconciliation among peoples serves peace and a united continent (Internationalism). Parties of the centre unite believers and moderates in broad coalitions that build the welfare state through parliamentary majorities and the integration of Europe. Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a labour party shaped by the church seeks change through the ballot. Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that the better-off bear the cost of justice. Public life is subordinated to revealed doctrine and the church's moral teaching, because religious tradition is the oldest guide to the good of society.

Compassionate Conservatism.d: The state and charities look after the welfare, habits and moral growth of citizens through guidance, because conservatives owe aid to the poor who struggle (Civic Paternalism). Established institutions, family and gradual change are preferred, since faith-based associations and local communities strengthen people better than distant bureaucracies (Conservatism). Compassion is shown through personal responsibility, family, faith groups and neighbourhood charities that work beside government, because lasting help comes from people who know the poor by name.

Rockefeller Republicanism.d: Enterprise, property rights and respect for established order go together with moderate social programmes, since a conservative who accepts markets can govern by balance and not by ideology (Liberal Conservatism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions advances American interests, since alliances and multilateral bodies sustain stability (Internationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that bargaining in legislatures produces broad consensus (Representative Democracy).

Democratic Transhumanism.d: Technology should enhance human intellect, health and lifespan through genetic engineering and cybernetics, because every person deserves access to longer and better lives (Transhumanism). A basic income funded within a capitalist economy gives each citizen security, since technological abundance lets markets coexist with a guaranteed floor (Basic Income Capitalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that democratic oversight guides powerful technologies (Representative Democracy). Faith in advance through science and reform leads society to improve the human condition, because enhancement serves emancipation (Progressivism). Global free trade and open borders spread the benefits of new technology, since knowledge flows across countries (Globalism). A single human community with a shared morality beyond nations includes enhanced and unenhanced alike, because rights belong to every sentient person (Cosmopolitanism).

Neo-Solidarism.d: The economy serves cooperatives, mutual societies and community enterprises that put people above profit, since solidarity networks give citizens control over their livelihoods (Social Solidarity Economy). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand social equality, because solidarity means protecting minorities and the vulnerable (Social-Progressivism). Technological innovation and efficient production are used to decouple growth from environmental harm, so that clean energy and high yields serve both people and nature (Ecomodernism). Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation and renewable energy is needed, since solidarity extends to future generations (Environmentalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions answers shared problems, because climate and poverty cross borders (Internationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that public deliberation shapes solidarity policies (Representative Democracy).

Steppe Eurasianism.d: Social identity and loyalty are anchored in great civilizational spheres, because the nomadic and continental peoples of the steppe form a world apart from the maritime West (Civilizationism). Global free trade and open borders are rejected since the market of sea powers would dissolve the continent's own heartland order (against Globalism). Profits and rents of state-owned enterprises supply the main revenue of the state, so that the common resources of the heartland remain with the ruler and the people (State Enterprise Revenue).

Classical Kemalism.d: The state exerts directive influence over investment and the founding of national industry, because planned development after the war builds a new republic (Dirigisme). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, since all who live in the republic are Turks by civic bond (Civic Nationalism). Faith in advance through science and reform drives modernization, so that old institutions give way to a rational republic (Progressivism). Factories, railways and large-scale manufacturing expand material abundance, because industrial strength secures independence (Industrialism). A worldview grounding ethics in reason and human dignity without revelation shapes public life, since schools and law are secular (Secular Humanism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because the caliphate and the sharia court must give way to the republic (against Theocracy). A ruler who legitimizes power as defender of a religion is rejected, since religious authority must not command the state (against Religious Authoritarianism). A sultan with absolute power is rejected because sovereignty belongs to the nation (against Absolute Monarchy). A monarch with unlimited power is rejected because arbitrary rule violates the rights of Englishmen.

Centrist Kemalism.d: Belonging comes from loyalty to the republic and its constitution, since every citizen who accepts its principles is a Turk whatever their descent (Civic Nationalism). Authority is concentrated in Ankara, because a unitary state with provinces as mere administrative divisions applies one law and one secular order everywhere (Centralism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that the assembly in Ankara expresses the national will (Representative Democracy). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected since the republic's laws must come from the nation and not from religious authority (against Theocracy). Administrative authority is concentrated in Ankara, because a unitary state carries the reforms to every province. Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because the caliphate and the sharia court must give way to the republic. Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because the republic's law must come from the people. The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, so that the republic's solidarity belongs to every resident who adheres to it. Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected since the republic's laws must be secular and made by the nation.

Catholic Social Teaching.d: Society is a community of mutual obligation, because the dignity of the person unfolds in family, parish and neighbourhood and not in isolation (Communitarianism). The state protects the welfare, health and living conditions of citizens through guidance and benefits, since the common good includes a just wage and care for the weak (Civic Paternalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions is supported, because the universal church teaches that the human family is one (Internationalism). Nature is respected and protected from destruction, since creation is a gift entrusted to humanity (Conservationism). Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation is required, so that stewardship of the earth serves present and future generations (Environmentalism). Free markets without moral limits are rejected because profit alone treats workers as commodities (against Laissez-Faire). Class-war revolution is rejected since it sets one group against another and denies private property and the family (against Communization). State ownership with central planning is rejected, because the state would swallow families and associations (against State Socialism).

Bleeding-Heart Authoritarianism.d: A single ruler holds absolute power to enforce humane goals, because a decisive leader can impose reforms that quarrelling parties would block (Autocracy). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government, since a unitary state applies relief evenly across the country (Centralism). Consensual adult conduct and lifestyle choices are left alone, so that tolerance in private life accompanies strong rule in public affairs (Permissivism). Faith in advance through science and reform guides the ruler, because compassion demands improvement of human conditions (Progressivism). A benevolent and reforming government rules firmly yet kindly, extending health care, schooling and personal tolerance by decree, in the manner of enlightened liberal modernizers who accept a strong executive. One leader holds unrestrained power over the state, because firm command can keep a free economy and social order together. Faith in advance through science and reform guides government, since liberal policy should improve human conditions by design. Faith in advance through science and reform leads society to improve the human condition, because enhancement serves emancipation. Global free trade and open borders are welcomed since they lift the world's poor through work and exchange. Consensual adult activities, lifestyle choices and morally controversial behaviour are tolerated, since the acquisitive person's pleasures harm no one else.

Austro-Corporatism.d: Wages and policy are settled among the state, employers and unions through standing chambers of social partners, because consensus between representative bodies keeps the economy stable (Neocorporatism). The republic keeps a modest army while refusing to join military blocs, since permanent neutrality protects a small state's independence (Armed Neutrality). Chambers of labour, commerce and agriculture negotiate with ministers and with each other, so that every large interest sits at the table and policy is made by agreement before it reaches parliament.

Davos System.d: A market in which firms, banks and workers cooperate for the long term is favoured, because stakeholder capitalism balances profit with society (Rhine Capitalism). A politics beyond old left and right combines market dynamism with social investment, since modern governance enables people to adapt (Third Way). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that wealth funds inclusion (Progressive Taxation). Faith in advance through science and reform guides global policy, because innovation can improve the human condition (Progressivism). The protection of individual rights and expression is part of an open society, since freedom enables enterprise (Civil Liberalism). Rule by trained specialists chosen for competence guides complex systems, because experts in forums and institutions coordinate global problems (Technocracy). A single human community with a morality beyond nations underlies the project, since challenges cross borders (Cosmopolitanism). Global free trade and open borders are advanced, because integrated supply chains and capital flows spread prosperity (Globalism). Economy and life move toward knowledge and digital services, since the fourth industrial revolution reshapes work (Post-Industrialism). Technological innovation is used to decouple growth from environmental harm, so that clean technology serves both people and planet (Ecomodernism). The state looks after the health, skills and living conditions of citizens through public provision and partnership, because inclusion keeps societies stable (Civic Paternalism). Power is shared between levels of government, since global, national and local bodies cooperate (Federalism). The country staying apart from foreign entanglements is rejected because isolation costs growth and security (against Isolationism). The nation defined by ethnicity is rejected, since belonging cannot depend on descent (against Ethnic Nationalism). The nation defined by race is rejected because the dignity of persons is universal (against Racial Nationalism). A market free of regulation is rejected, since unchecked capitalism harms trust and the climate (against Laissez-Faire). The abolition of rulers is rejected because institutions are needed to coordinate global affairs (against Anarchism).

Nordic Model.d: Wage and economic policy is settled among government, employers and unions in broad bargaining, because social partnership makes change acceptable (Neocorporatism). Tax rates that rise with income fund universal services, so that higher incomes carry more of the common cost (Progressive Taxation). The state looks after the health, education and living conditions of citizens from cradle to grave, since care for all secures equality of opportunity (Civic Paternalism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand gender and social equality, because rights for minorities and women are part of the welfare state (Social-Progressivism). A market in which firms, banks and workers cooperate for the long term is favoured, since stable ownership and employee voice outweigh short-term profit (Rhine Capitalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions serves small open economies, because rules protect them from power politics (Internationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that parliaments and consensus-seeking parties run the welfare state (Representative Democracy). Unions run the unemployment insurance and social benefits, because workers' organizations that deliver benefits keep membership high and wages bargained (Ghent System). A tax whose rate falls as income rises is rejected since it would burden ordinary earners and weaken the shared funding of services (against Regressive Taxation).

Social Democracy.d: A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and solidarity insurance, because regulated capitalism gives growth and fairness together (Social Market). Taxes climb with income so that those with most ability to pay fund the public services, since equality of opportunity needs resources (Progressive Taxation). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that reform is won gradually through democratic majorities (Representative Democracy). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand social equality, because the labour movement defends minorities and the vulnerable (Social-Progressivism). The state looks after health, education and housing through public provision, since security for every citizen is a collective duty (Civic Paternalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies builds peace and labour standards, since workers' solidarity crosses borders (Internationalism). Public spending and deficits are used to stabilize demand and employment, because governments must steer the economy through slumps (Keynesianism). Free private markets without regulation are rejected since the unrestrained market produces insecurity and inequality (against Laissez-Faire). A revolutionary break to abolish capitalism and the state is rejected, because lasting change comes through the ballot and reform (against Communization). A tax whose rate falls as income rises is rejected since it shifts the burden onto those with the least (against Regressive Taxation).

Conservative Social Democracy.d: Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, because social protection should be built on family, community and tradition rather than on rupture (Conservatism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since solidarity rests on neighbourhoods, churches and local ties (Communitarianism). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and solidarity insurance, so that markets work inside a framework of fair rules (Social Market). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because those who prosper owe a larger share to the common good (Progressive Taxation). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since moderate parliaments secure steady welfare reform (Representative Democracy).

Social Distributism.d: Property is widely shared through cooperatives, guilds and public funds that give working families a stake, since social ownership spreads capital among citizens (Social-Distributism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, because families and associations bind members to shared duties (Communitarianism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that excess wealth is redirected to broaden ownership (Progressive Taxation). Productive property is spread among many households and small owners, since a society of independent proprietors resists both monopoly and bureaucracy (Distributism). A different global order of fair trade among peoples and communities is sought, because the world economy should serve workers and localities and not capital (Alter-Globalism). A market free of regulation is rejected since concentrated capital swallows small owners (against Laissez-Faire). State ownership run by central planners is rejected because it replaces the household's property with officials (against State Socialism).

Eurocommunism.d: Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because socialism is reached through the parliamentary road and pluralist elections (Representative Democracy). The protection of individual rights and expression, including freedom of the press, is kept in a socialist state, since democracy and liberty are part of the transformation (Civil Liberalism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that public spending and social reform advance gradually (Progressive Taxation). One party dominating the state apparatus is rejected because a single ruling party suppresses the pluralism that socialism needs (against Partocracy).

Liberal Socialism.d: Firms are owned and run by their workers within competitive markets, because market socialism joins collective ownership with prices and choice (Market Socialism). The protection of individual rights and expression is guaranteed, since socialism without freedom becomes domination (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that public enterprise answers to democratic assemblies (Representative Democracy). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because equal opportunity needs a fair distribution of resources (Progressive Taxation). Profits and rents of state-owned enterprises provide public revenue, since common ownership of key assets funds social goods (State Enterprise Revenue). One party dominating the state is rejected because a single ruling party ends political competition (against Partocracy). The absorption of the person into the state is rejected, since no private sphere can be left to officials alone (against Totalism).

Social Georgism.d: Land is taxed on its unimproved site value, because the rent from nature belongs to the whole community and not to owners (Land Value Tax). A tax on land holdings by area and use falls on those who hold large estates, since idle land should carry a charge (Mixed Land Tax). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity, so that public revenue from land funds social insurance (Social Market). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, because the community that creates land values should share them (Social-Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since democratic assemblies set the land charge and spend its proceeds (Representative Democracy).

Agrarian Social Democracy.d: Farming and rural settlement are the foundation of a healthy society, because family farms and village life give the working countryside security and dignity (Agrarianism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since farmers, cooperatives and parishes carry one another through bad harvests (Communitarianism). Property is shared through cooperatives, mutual funds and smallholder grants that give rural households a stake, so that land and credit do not concentrate in few hands (Social-Distributism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because urban wealth should support rural schools, roads and pensions (Progressive Taxation). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since peasant parties win reform in parliament through coalition (Representative Democracy).

Progressive Corporatism.d: Wages and policy are settled among the state, employers and unions in standing bodies, because organized interests that bargain for the common good give lasting social peace (Neocorporatism). A market in which firms, banks and workers cooperate for the long term is favoured, so that codetermination in boards outweighs short-term profit (Rhine Capitalism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and widen equality, since the corporate partners must include women and minorities (Social-Progressivism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because fair shares keep the compact between classes stable (Progressive Taxation). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that chambers of interests stay accountable to parliament (Representative Democracy). Trades and professions are grouped into functional bodies of workers and employers, since representation by sector gives each its own voice (Corporatism). Unions administer unemployment insurance and benefits, because workers' organizations that deliver welfare keep membership high and bargaining strong (Ghent System).

Left-Gaullism.d: The state steers investment and key sectors with directive influence, because planning, nationalized industry and public credit protect independence (Dirigisme). The country keeps its own strong military while refusing blocs, since armed neutrality keeps it from serving a superpower (Armed Neutrality). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, so that the republic's solidarity belongs to every resident who adheres to it (Civic Nationalism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because the Republic's social contract requires fair contribution from the wealthy (Progressive Taxation). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since a grand national project must include the excluded (Social-Progressivism).

Labour Atlanticism.d: Public spending and deficits are used to stabilize demand and employment, because the state must manage the economy to secure full work after the war (Keynesianism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, since a fair share pays for health and welfare (Progressive Taxation). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, because the labour movement defends the vulnerable (Social-Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that a parliamentary party wins power through the ballot (Representative Democracy). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in the Western alliance, since a transatlantic community of democracies stands against the Soviet bloc (Civilizationism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies, including the alliance and the United Nations, secures peace (Internationalism).

Green Social Democracy.d: Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation and renewable energy is needed, because the climate crisis demands a just transition for workers (Environmentalism). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and solidarity insurance, so that green investment is fair to every household (Social Market). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, since carbon pricing and public investment must fall hardest on the rich (Progressive Taxation). The state looks after health, housing and mobility through public services, because collective provision protects people from ecological and economic shocks (Civic Paternalism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since the ecological transition must leave no one behind (Social-Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that climate policy has democratic legitimacy (Representative Democracy). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is needed, because pollution and warming cross borders (Internationalism). The state looks after health, education and housing through public provision, since security for every citizen is a collective duty.

Geo-Social Democracy.d: Land is taxed on its unimproved site value, because the community creates the worth of location and should collect it (Land Value Tax). A tax on landholdings by size and use falls on large and idle estates, since speculation in property should pay its way (Mixed Land Tax). The state looks after health, housing and education from the land revenue, so that every citizen shares the common inheritance (Civic Paternalism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, because rent captured for all lifts the poor first (Social-Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since parliaments decide the rate and the dividend (Representative Democracy).

Christian Social Democracy.d: Society is a community of mutual obligation, because the neighbour's need is a duty of faith and fellowship (Communitarianism). The state protects the welfare, health and living conditions of citizens through public provision, since the Gospel calls for care of the poor and sick (Civic Paternalism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that the better-off bear the cost of justice (Progressive Taxation). Cooperatives, mutual aid societies and community enterprises that put people above profit are built, because solidarity among believers organizes the economy for the common good (Social Solidarity Economy). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a labour party shaped by the church seeks change through the ballot (Representative Democracy).

Police Labourism.d: Preventive policing, data collection and surveillance preserve safety in working-class neighbourhoods, because crime falls hardest on the poor and must be stopped early (Securitism). The state looks after the welfare and living conditions of citizens through public services, since a strong labour government protects its voters (Civic Paternalism). Crime is answered by proportionate punishment as just desert, so that offenders pay for what they did (Retributivism). Order kept by peer accountability and community ostracism instead of police is rejected, because neighbourhoods need a visible force with authority (against Reputationalism).

Ecevitism.d: Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because a democratic left of the people must ease the load on workers and villagers (Progressive Taxation). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since the left of the centre opens the republic to peasants and workers (Social-Progressivism). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, so that every citizen of the republic belongs without regard to origin (Civic Nationalism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because a secular republic must keep faith out of the state (against Theocracy).

Left-Social Authoritarianism.d: One leader holds absolute personal power to carry out reforms for the working majority, because decisive command overcomes the blocking of elites (Autocracy). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, since heavy contribution from wealth funds social programmes (Progressive Taxation). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government, so that a unitary state delivers the same benefits to every region (Centralism). The state looks after the housing, health and work of citizens through guidance, because the ruler secures welfare as a duty (Civic Paternalism). The state steers investment and key sectors with directive influence, since national plans direct production for the people (Dirigisme). Profits and rents of state-owned enterprises supply the main public revenue, because the nation's enterprises belong to the people and fund their services (State Enterprise Revenue). One leader holds unchecked power to modernize society, because a decisive ruler can push through science, schooling and reform against resistance. A single ruler holds absolute power to enforce humane goals, because a decisive leader can impose reforms that quarrelling parties would block. One ruler holds personal power without effective restraint, since elections only confirm the incumbent. Administrative authority is concentrated in the capital, because appointed governors keep regions in line. One leader holds absolute power without restraint, since a dictator can end the chaos of the revolution. Administrative authority is concentrated in Moscow, since a vertical of power makes regions executors of the centre. One leader holds absolute power without restraint, because the helmsman embodies the will of the people.

Progressive Social Authoritarianism.d: One leader holds unchecked power to modernize society, because a decisive ruler can push through science, schooling and reform against resistance (Autocracy). Faith in advance through science and social reform guides the state, since history moves toward a better order (Progressivism). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government, so that a unitary state can impose uniform standards (Centralism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because the wealthy must pay for the new order (Progressive Taxation). The state exerts strong directive influence over investment and key sectors, since planned development advances the people (Dirigisme). Profits and rents of state enterprises provide the main revenue, so that public ownership funds welfare and growth (State Enterprise Revenue). Preserving established institutions and gradual change is rejected because inherited habits hold back improvement (against Conservatism).

Left-Wing Populism.d: Citizens vote directly on laws and policies through referendums and initiatives, because the ordinary people should decide rather than a distant political class (Referendum Democracy). Very high taxes take wealth and income above a ceiling, since the economic elite has taken more than its share (Confiscatory Taxation). A different global order of fair trade among peoples is sought, because the world economy should serve workers and not multinational capital (Alter-Globalism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, so that the people's movement includes the vulnerable (Social-Progressivism). A market free of regulation is rejected since the unrestricted pursuit of private profit enriches the few at the expense of the many (against Laissez-Faire). Global free trade and open borders that serve financial interests are rejected because they weaken the bargaining power of working people (against Globalism).

Left-Social Democracy.d: Firms are owned and run by workers within competitive markets, because the future of the economy lies in collective ownership joined with choice (Market Socialism). Very high taxes take wealth and income above a ceiling, since steep levies on the top are needed to rein in inequality (Confiscatory Taxation). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, because the democratic left extends rights to minorities and women (Social-Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that socialism is built by parliamentary majorities (Representative Democracy). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since neighbours and workplaces share risks and responsibilities (Communitarianism). A different global order of fair trade among peoples and communities is sought, because the world economy should serve workers and not capital (Alter-Globalism). The state looks after health, housing and education through public services, since collective provision guarantees universal care (Civic Paternalism).

Social-Helveticism.d: Citizens vote directly on laws and policies through referendums and initiatives, because the Swiss people hold sovereignty and settle questions at the ballot box (Referendum Democracy). Power is shared between the federal government and cantons, since each canton keeps its own authority and a limited union serves them (Federalism). The country keeps strong defence through a militia while staying out of alliances, because neutrality is the pledge of independence (Armed Neutrality). The state looks after the welfare of citizens through public insurance and services, so that the community secures pensions and health for every resident (Civic Paternalism). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship rather than ethnicity, because a Swiss identity binds four languages and many cantons (Civic Nationalism). Rule by a small elite that governs for its own gain is rejected since the people's direct vote guards against capture (against Oligarchy).

Left Kemalism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because the republic's founding principle of public ownership in key sectors protects the nation (State Socialism). Firms are owned and run by workers within competitive markets, since the working people of the republic should gain a share in management (Market Socialism). Profits of state-owned enterprises supply the main revenue of the budget, so that public enterprises fund schools and roads (State Enterprise Revenue). Very high taxes take wealth and income above a ceiling, because extreme fortunes must be reduced for the common good (Confiscatory Taxation). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since women's rights and secular reform are the heritage of the revolution (Social-Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because the grand national assembly is the home of popular sovereignty (Representative Democracy). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, since every citizen of the republic is a Turk by civic bond (Civic Nationalism). The country keeps a strong military while refusing blocs, because peace at home and abroad protects the republic (Armed Neutrality). Factories and heavy industry expand material abundance, so that industrialization frees workers from poverty (Industrialism). The state looks after the education, health and living conditions of citizens, since the republic has social duties (Civic Paternalism). Administrative authority is concentrated in Ankara, because a unitary state applies the same law everywhere (Centralism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since private profit would take the republic's wealth (against Laissez-Faire). Rule by clergy under divine law is rejected because the republic is secular (against Theocracy). The nation defined by ethnicity is rejected, since the republic belongs to all its citizens (against Ethnic Nationalism). The nation bound by one religion is rejected because faith must not define citizenship (against Religious Nationalism).

Longism.d: Public spending and deficits are used to stabilize demand and employment, because government must put purchasing power in the hands of the poor (Keynesianism). Employers owe a duty of care toward their employees and the community, since firms that share wealth and look after their workers keep enterprise honest (Paternalistic Capitalism). Very high taxes take wealth and income above a ceiling, so that every family has a homestead and a basic living (Confiscatory Taxation). Pragmatic reform within the tradition is accepted, because a populist movement can adapt the old order to relieve the poor (Progressive Conservatism). Elected representatives and legislators chosen by the voters govern on behalf of citizens, since every poor man must keep his ballot and a seat at the table of lawmaking (Representative Democracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, because every man is a king and every citizen has a place in the republic (Civic Nationalism). The country stays out of foreign entanglements, since the wealth of the nation should be shared at home (Isolationism). Ideas and doctrines are judged by practical usefulness as tools for the people's welfare, since a policy is sound when it works for the poor and not by its theory (Instrumentalism). The state looks after the schooling, roads and health of citizens through public provision, because the commonwealth owes a living to all (Civic Paternalism). Power is shared between the federal government and the states, since a state may act on its own for its people (Federalism). An economy free of government intervention is rejected, since private transactions without public rules let a few hoard wealth while the many go hungry (against Laissez-Faire). Power belonging to a ruling class of inherited status is rejected, since a few families should not hold the land and the money (against Aristocracy). A tax whose rate falls as income rises is rejected because it burdens the working family (against Regressive Taxation).

Classical Liberalism.d: An economy free of government intervention rewards effort and lets prices guide production, because voluntary exchange among owners spreads prosperity (Laissez-Faire). The protection of individual rights and expression, including freedom of conscience, speech and the press, is the purpose of government (Civil Liberalism). The state is limited to protecting life, liberty and property, so that its power does not exceed night-watchman duties (Minarchism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens under a constitution, since consent and limits keep authority accountable (Representative Democracy). The country avoids alliances and wars abroad, because peace and commerce with all nations suit free people (Non-Interventionism). Safeguarding personal privacy, speech and due process against state power is essential, since liberty means protection from arbitrary arrest (Civil Libertarianism). A monarch with unlimited power is rejected because no ruler may stand above the law and the consent of the governed (against Absolute Monarchy). State ownership with central planning is rejected, since it ends property and personal liberty (against State Socialism). Rule by clergy under divine law is rejected because conscience cannot be coerced by the state (against Theocracy). Revenue from state-owned enterprises is rejected, since government should not run commerce (against State Enterprise Revenue). Workplaces run through councils of workers and consumers are rejected because collective planning replaces voluntary contracts (against Participatory Economics).

Neoliberalism.d: Free markets, privatization and competition allocate resources best, because deregulation unlocks growth that state planning cannot match (Laissez-Faire). Government provides only a basic safety net, since welfare beyond a minimum dulls incentives and swells public budgets (Residualism). Global free trade and open borders spread capital and goods, because integrated markets lift living standards worldwide (Globalism). The protection of individual rights and expression goes with economic choice, so that people are free consumers and owners (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since stable constitutional politics is the framework for market order (Representative Democracy). State ownership and central planning are rejected because they distort prices and shield inefficient industry (against State Socialism). Government steering of investment and key sectors is rejected, since industrial policy picks losers and invites lobbying (against Dirigisme). Tariffs and managed trade to build national wealth are rejected because protection raises prices and shrinks exports (against Mercantilism).

National Liberalism.d: An economy free of state intervention drives the nation's prosperity, because private enterprise and open exchange build national strength (Laissez-Faire).
