Liberty is preserved together with established institutions and moral order, since a nation's freedoms rest on tradition and constitutional continuity (Conservative Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that the liberal state is anchored in parliament and the rule of law (Representative Democracy). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, because liberal freedoms need a unified people to protect them (Cultural Nationalism).  Liberal institutions are strongest where citizens share a language and a history, and the state exists to guard both the liberties and the common life of its people.

Social Liberalism.d: A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and universal solidarity insurance, because real freedom needs education, health and a fair start (Social Market). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, since public provision of opportunity must be paid for by those who gain most (Progressive Taxation). The protection of individual rights and expression is the core of the creed, so that every person can pursue their own life (Civil Liberalism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, since liberty includes protection from surveillance (Civil Libertarianism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because reform within constitutional order secures equal rights (Representative Democracy). Unregulated markets are rejected because poverty and monopoly limit the freedom of the poor (against Laissez-Faire). The protection of individual rights and expression is kept together with economic security, so that liberty means freedom from want.

Ordoliberalism.d: The state sets the rules of the economic order and enforces competition, because a strong legal framework prevents cartels and keeps markets fair (Ordnungspolitik). Liberty is joined with established institutions, price stability and moral responsibility, since a free economy rests on a stable constitutional order (Conservative Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens through accountable parliaments, so that the constitutional rules of the economic order rest on consent and answer to voters (Representative Democracy). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and solidarity insurance, because a competitive order must also give security to all (Social Market). An economy free of state intervention is rejected since a market left to itself without government rules breeds cartels and destroys competition (against Laissez-Faire). State ownership with central planning is rejected, because it replaces competition and prices with officials (against State Socialism).

Bleeding-Heart Liberalism.d: A basic income is paid to every citizen within a capitalist economy, because a guaranteed floor expands freedom while markets still reward work (Basic Income Capitalism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since compassion for the vulnerable is the purpose of a liberal state (Social-Progressivism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, so that civil liberty and welfare support each other (Civil Libertarianism). A single human community with a shared morality beyond nations commands equal concern for every person, because borders are morally arbitrary (Cosmopolitanism). Global free trade and open borders lift the poorest people, since migration and commerce are routes out of poverty (Globalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that humane policy is won through democratic politics (Representative Democracy).

Bleeding-Heart Libertarianism.d: The state is limited to a minimal night-watchman role, because coercion beyond the protection of rights wrongs the poor as much as the rich (Minarchism). Free markets without government intervention serve the least advantaged best, since open competition and enterprise raise their living standards (Laissez-Faire). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, so that liberty is also a shield for outsiders and minorities (Civil Libertarianism). A single human community with a shared morality beyond nations deserves equal concern, because arbitrary borders deny the poor their right to move and trade (Cosmopolitanism). Global free trade and open borders are welcomed since they lift the world's poor through work and exchange (Globalism).

Geo-Liberalism.d: Land is taxed on its unimproved site value, because the rent of nature belongs to everyone while labour and capital keep their earnings (Land Value Tax). A tax on landholdings by area and use discourages idle estates, since speculation in property should pay its way (Mixed Land Tax). A basic income paid from land rents gives each citizen a share of the common inheritance within a capitalist economy, so that a market society is also a fair one (Basic Income Capitalism). The protection of individual rights and expression is secured for all, because liberty needs equal access to land (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a free republic sets the charge on land by consent (Representative Democracy).

Green Liberalism.d: Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation, pricing of pollution and renewable energy is needed, because clean air and a stable climate are conditions of liberty (Environmentalism). The protection of individual rights and expression is the core of the creed, so that every person may live, speak and choose freely in a sustainable society (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since ecological policy needs democratic consent (Representative Democracy). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and universal insurance, because competition within ecological limits serves everyone (Social Market). Global free trade and open borders spread clean technology, since open markets and exchange of ideas speed the shift to sustainability (Globalism).

Whiggism.d: A crown whose powers are limited by a constitution and parliament secures liberty, because the settlement of the revolution keeps the monarch under the law (Constitutional Monarchy). Liberty is preserved together with established institutions and property, since reform must grow from the ancient constitution and not from upheaval (Conservative Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that parliament, led by landed gentlemen and merchants, guards the people's rights (Representative Democracy). A monarch with unlimited power is rejected because arbitrary rule violates the rights of Englishmen (against Absolute Monarchy). Rule by the passions of the mob is rejected, since a government subject to the crowd threatens property and order (against Ochlocracy).

Muscular Liberalism.d: The protection of individual rights and expression is defended with confidence and not apology, because liberal society must stand up for its own values (Civil Liberalism). Democratic states use force and diplomacy in other countries to defend freedom, since tyranny abroad endangers liberty at home (Interventionism). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, so that newcomers are expected to adopt the common values of the country (Cultural Nationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because the law of the democratic state sets the limit of tolerance (Representative Democracy).

Liberal Atlanticism.d: The protection of individual rights and expression binds the transatlantic world, because liberty and the rule of law are the common inheritance of Western democracies (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that allied parliaments hold power accountable (Representative Democracy). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in the Western alliance of democracies, since its shared civilization faces authoritarian rivals (Civilizationism). Democratic states use their power in other countries when needed, because defending the liberal order demands diplomacy and force (Interventionism). Personal privacy, speech and due process are guarded against state power, since security measures must not erode freedom (Civil Libertarianism).

Transatlantic Federalism.d: Sovereignty is shared between a federal government and constituent states, because a union of Atlantic democracies pools power while members keep their own authority (Federalism). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in a Western civilization, since one community of liberal nations shares history and values (Civilizationism). Global free trade and open borders connect the allied economies, so that exchange of goods, people and capital binds the alliance (Globalism). The protection of individual rights and expression is guaranteed across the union, because liberty is its founding commitment (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a federal legislature chosen by voters gives the union legitimacy (Representative Democracy). Sovereignty is shared between a federal level and constituent members, because nested layers of self-rule fit a networked world.

New Deal Liberalism.d: Public spending and deficits are used to stabilize demand and employment, because government must act to end the depression and restore work (Keynesianism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, since the prosperous should fund relief and public works (Progressive Taxation). The protection of individual rights and expression is kept together with economic security, so that liberty means freedom from want (Civil Liberalism). The state looks after the welfare, pensions and jobs of citizens through federal programmes, because collective provision protects people from market collapse (Civic Paternalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that legislation by a reforming majority reshapes the economy (Representative Democracy). An economy left free of government rules is rejected since unregulated markets brought the collapse (against Laissez-Faire).

Venizelism.d: Liberty is preserved together with established institutions and a modern constitution, because a progressive monarchy-republic order can combine reform with stability (Conservative Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a liberal parliament carries the national cause (Representative Democracy). All people of Greek language and descent should be united into one state across existing borders, so that the Great Idea gathers the nation (Pan-Nationalism). The country extends its power over other territories by diplomacy and force, since expansion after the wars secures national greatness (Imperialism). Territories inhabited by compatriots under foreign rule are claimed for the homeland, because unredeemed lands belong to the nation (Irredentism).

Liberal Kemalism.d: The protection of individual rights and expression is part of the republic's reforms, because citizens are free and equal under law (Civil Liberalism). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, since every resident of the republic is a Turk by civic bond (Civic Nationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that the national assembly speaks for the people (Representative Democracy). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, because liberty must limit even a republican state (Civil Libertarianism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected since the republic's laws must be secular and made by the nation (against Theocracy). Safeguarding personal privacy, speech and due process against state power is essential, since liberty means protection from arbitrary arrest. The protection of individual rights and expression, including freedom of conscience, speech and the press, is the purpose of government.

Liberal Social Authoritarianism.d: One leader holds unrestrained power over the state, because firm command can keep a free economy and social order together (Autocracy). Safeguarding personal privacy, speech and due process against the state is rejected, since liberty claims must give way to the ruler's decisions (against Civil Libertarianism). Each citizen is left free to trade and live as they choose within the limits the ruler sets, because order and enterprise go together under strong guidance. Schooling, public safety and welfare are organized from above, since a firm state that guarantees property and contracts lets commerce flourish without political disorder.

Techno-Social Liberalism.d: Economy and daily life move toward knowledge, services and information, because digital and scientific work create the new wealth and demand new public investment (Post-Industrialism). A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and universal insurance, since a fair start lets everyone take part in the digital economy (Social Market). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that gains from technology are shared (Progressive Taxation). Faith in advance through science and reform leads policy, because technology can improve the human condition (Progressivism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state and corporate power, since data protection is a form of liberty (Civil Libertarianism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that rules for platforms are set democratically (Representative Democracy). Global free trade and open borders spread knowledge and talent, because networks cross frontiers (Globalism).

Technoliberalism.d: Economy and daily life move away from manufacturing toward information, software and services, because networks and data are the new factories (Post-Industrialism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, since encryption and open networks protect the individual (Civil Libertarianism). The protection of individual rights and expression is the core of the creed, so that people are free to publish, build and associate online (Civil Liberalism). Global free trade and open borders let data, capital and talent cross frontiers, because a connected world widens opportunity (Globalism). A single human community with a shared morality beyond nations is the horizon, since the internet joins people of every country (Cosmopolitanism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that technology is held under the rule of law (Representative Democracy).

American Model.d: Power is shared between the federal government and the states, because dividing sovereignty protects liberty from concentrated authority (Federalism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, since the Bill of Rights restrains the government (Civil Libertarianism). The protection of individual rights and expression is the national creed, so that each person may pursue happiness (Civil Liberalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because Congress and checks and balances turn consent into law (Representative Democracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship rather than ethnicity, since the American creed gives every immigrant a place (Civic Nationalism). Democratic states use force and diplomacy in other countries when needed, because the leader of the free world defends its allies and its interests (Interventionism). Government provides only a basic safety net, since individual initiative and private charity should carry most of social need (Residualism).

Techno-Neoliberalism.d: Rule by trained specialists and experts chosen for competence guides policy, because complex systems need technical knowledge more than popular opinion (Technocracy). Global free trade and open borders connect markets, since data, platforms and capital flow best without barriers (Globalism). The economy shifts from manufacturing toward information and services, so that software and platforms generate the wealth (Post-Industrialism). Free markets without government intervention reward innovation, because competition among firms drives progress faster than regulation (Laissez-Faire). A single human community with shared morality beyond nations is assumed, since the digital economy treats every user alike (Cosmopolitanism). Rule driven by mass passions is rejected because the crowd cannot judge technical questions (against Ochlocracy).

Tsaingwenism.d: A politics beyond old left and right combines market dynamism with social investment, because a modern government should enable its people to work, learn and compete (Third Way). Faith in advance through science and reform guides policy, since the island's future depends on innovation and equal rights (Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that a hard-won democracy is defended at the ballot box (Representative Democracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, because Taiwanese identity is built by those who live in the democracy and not by ancestry (Civic Nationalism). Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation and renewable energy is needed, since the island must move off fossil fuels (Environmentalism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, because freedom distinguishes the island from authoritarian neighbours (Civil Libertarianism). Global free trade and open borders tie the economy to the world, since integration into supply chains secures its prosperity (Globalism).

Liberal Imperialism.d: An economy free of state intervention drives trade, because commerce under the flag carries prosperity abroad (Laissez-Faire). The state sets the rules of the economic order and enforces fair competition, since a well-governed market underpins the imperial economy (Ordnungspolitik). Liberty is joined with established institutions and moral responsibility, so that civilizing rule combines freedom with order (Conservative Liberalism). The protection of individual rights and expression is a mission of the empire, because rule of law is the gift it brings (Civil Liberalism). Market institutions and established order are respected together, since a conservative framework carries the imperial project (Liberal Conservatism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens at home, so that parliament authorizes the imperial effort (Representative Democracy). Offices and rewards go to those with ability and merit, because a trained civil service governs distant provinces (Meritocracy). The nation is bound by shared culture and language, since the mother country spreads its civilization (Cultural Nationalism). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, so that loyal subjects of every race may share its ideals (Civic Nationalism). The country extends its power and dominance over other territories through force and diplomacy, because a great liberal power has a duty to spread order and trade (Imperialism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded at home against state power, since liberty is the pride of the metropolis (Civil Libertarianism). Staying apart from foreign entanglements is rejected because a trading power cannot retreat (against Isolationism). Opposing war and militarism is rejected, since the fleet and army secure the empire (against Pacifism). A revolution that abolishes classes and property is rejected because it ends commerce and law (against Communization). State ownership with central planning is rejected, since private enterprise opens the world to trade (against State Socialism).

Liberal Meritocracy.d: A market economy is combined with guarantees of social equity and solidarity insurance, because competition needs a fair starting line for every child (Social Market). A politics beyond old left and right combines market dynamism with social investment, since opportunity for talent must be widened (Third Way). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that public goods in schooling and health pay for equal chances (Progressive Taxation). The protection of individual rights and expression is the base of the order, because each person is free to develop their ability (Civil Liberalism). Offices and rewards go to those with proven ability and merit, since a fair contest of talent, not birth or favour, decides who leads (Meritocracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, because talented people of every origin belong to it (Civic Nationalism). Democratic states use force and diplomacy in other countries when needed, so that an open order is defended (Interventionism). Global free trade and open borders spread talent and capital, since exchange rewards skill wherever it appears (Globalism). Economy and life move toward knowledge, services and information, because education is the new capital (Post-Industrialism). Technological innovation is used to decouple growth from environmental harm, since clever solutions serve both economy and nature (Ecomodernism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, because freedom of inquiry nourishes talent (Civil Libertarianism). Power is shared between levels of government, so that regions compete in policy (Federalism). Rule driven by mass passions is rejected because merit is trampled by demagogues (against Ochlocracy). Direct votes on laws through referendums are rejected, since complex questions are better decided by informed representatives (against Referendum Democracy). Withdrawing from world affairs is rejected because a meritocratic open society depends on global engagement (against Isolationism). One ruler with absolute power is rejected, since office must be earned and accountable (against Autocracy).

Christian Socialism.d: Society is a community of mutual obligation, because the teaching of Christ commands sharing and brotherhood among neighbours (Communitarianism). Idealistic cooperative communities built by voluntary association show the way to a just order, since moral persuasion and example can replace conflict (Utopian Socialism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, so that reform is sought through peaceful, democratic means (Representative Democracy). The country avoids wars and alliances abroad, because the gospel of peace forbids slaughter (Non-Interventionism). Free competition without regard for the poor is rejected since the pursuit of profit contradicts the command to love one's neighbour (against Laissez-Faire). A market free of regulation is rejected since unrestrained trade hollows out local shops, towns and old bonds.

National Bolshevism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy centrally, because collective ownership ends exploitation and builds national strength (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since common distribution replaces the market (Collective Distribution). One party leads the state apparatus and dominates politics, so that the vanguard guards the revolution and the nation (Partocracy). The nation is held together by shared culture, language and heritage, because the national tradition is the vessel of the revolution (Cultural Nationalism). The nation is a living spiritual community with its own soul and mythic past, since the people's destiny draws on legend and sacrifice (Romantic Nationalism). The revolutionary state expands its power and influence over other territories, because a great socialist power must dominate its sphere (Imperialism). A market free of state control is rejected since private capital serves foreign interests against the people (against Laissez-Faire). Elected representatives who govern for rival parties are rejected because parliamentary politics breeds corruption and weakness (against Representative Democracy). A single human community with a morality beyond nations is rejected, since the proletariat of each people must first free its own nation (against Cosmopolitanism).

Democratic Socialism.d: Firms are owned and run by workers within competitive markets, because collective ownership can go with prices and choice (Market Socialism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since socialism is won and kept through the ballot box (Representative Democracy). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, so that class justice includes women and minorities (Social-Progressivism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions links workers across borders, because international solidarity supports peace (Internationalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since unchecked capital dominates workers' lives (against Laissez-Faire). One party dominating the state apparatus is rejected because socialism without political pluralism turns into domination (against Partocracy). The absorption of the person into the state is rejected, since a private sphere must stay beyond the reach of officials (against Totalism).

Conservative Socialism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because the community should hold its common wealth for the sake of social order (State Socialism). Very high taxes take wealth and income above a ceiling, since steep levies on the top restore a fair society (Confiscatory Taxation). Gradual change and the preservation of established institutions are preferred, so that family and community survive economic reform (Conservatism). Inherited customs and natural obligations are preserved, because ownership by the community protects village and class traditions (Traditionalist Conservatism). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, since socialism belongs to a people with its own tradition (Cultural Nationalism). A market free of regulation is rejected because unchecked competition breaks communities and old ways of life (against Laissez-Faire). Faith in advance through reform and social engineering is rejected, since change for its own sake erodes the moral bonds of society (against Progressivism).

Paleosocialism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because the working people hold the nation's wealth in common (State Socialism). Authentic conservative values of faith, family and local tradition are defended against the elite, since the old customs of the working class deserve respect (Paleoconservatism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, so that neighbours, unions and churches support one another (Communitarianism). The country keeps out of foreign alliances and wars, because soldiers and money should serve workers at home (Isolationism). Very high taxes take wealth and income above a ceiling, since the economic elite must be reduced for the benefit of ordinary citizens (Confiscatory Taxation). The nation is defined by shared culture, language and heritage, because a common home gives the working class solidarity (Cultural Nationalism).

Cybernetic Socialism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy by feedback from computers, because networked planning can coordinate abundance for all (State Socialism). Rule by trained specialists chosen for competence manages systems, since complex flows of data need technical expertise (Technocracy). Citizens take part in decisions through online platforms and real-time voting, so that digital tools give every person a voice in planning (Digital Democracy). Humanity should gain total mastery over nature and scarcity through automation and computation, because machines can free everyone from toil (Prometheanism). Faith in advance through science and reform guides the project, since history moves toward rational coordination (Progressivism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is needed, because planning networks span the globe (Internationalism). The state steers investment and key sectors with strong directive influence, since feedback and plans guide production (Dirigisme). Planning of production through cybernetic socialism is the aim, so that information systems replace markets in meeting needs (Cybernetic Socialism).

Utopian Communitarianism.d: Idealistic model communities built on cooperation and shared life show a better society, because voluntary association and example can persuade without force (Utopian Socialism). Settlements share labour and goods in common households, since communal living ends rivalry and want (Communalism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, so that members care for one another as one family (Communitarianism). Faith in advance through science and reform leads the community, because education and invention improve human nature (Progressivism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since common distribution replaces buying and selling (Collective Distribution). Rule by a small elite that governs for its own gain is rejected because the colony's members decide together (against Oligarchy).

Syndicalist Republicanism.d: Workers' unions control the economy and its workplaces, because a republic of producers should be built from trade bodies and labour councils (Syndicalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since a republic keeps a parliament as the base of public rights (Representative Democracy). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, so that republican liberty includes all workers (Social-Progressivism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies links republics, because workers' solidarity crosses borders (Internationalism). A monarch with unlimited power is rejected since no crown may stand above a free people (against Absolute Monarchy). Delegates are chosen through trade syndicates and professional guilds, so that the producers who run each sector take part in government (Syndicracy).

Left-Eurasianism.d: Social identity and loyalty are anchored in great civilizational spheres, because the continental peoples of Eurasia form a united bloc against the Atlantic maritime powers (Civilizationism). The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, since common ownership of land and industry protects the heartland from market domination (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, so that shared provision binds the peoples of the continent in solidarity (Collective Distribution). A different global order of multipolar trade among regions and peoples is sought, because the world economy should serve continents and not a single financial centre (Alter-Globalism). One party dominating the state apparatus gives the project continuity, since a leading organization holds the continent's peoples together against external pressure (Partocracy).

Socialist Kemalism.d: The state owns and runs the key means of production, because the republic's etatism builds heavy industry for a nation without capitalists (State Socialism). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, since every citizen of the republic belongs to a people without privilege of class (Civic Nationalism). Factories, mines and railways expand material abundance, so that large-scale manufacturing makes the country independent (Industrialism). Administrative authority is concentrated in Ankara, because a unitary state carries the reforms to every province (Centralism). Faith in advance through science and reform leads the republic, since secular schooling and planning lift the peasantry (Progressivism). The state exerts directive influence over investment through five-year plans, so that national development is planned (Dirigisme). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because the republic's law must come from the people (against Theocracy).

Socialist Technoliberalism.d: Firms are owned and run by workers within competitive markets, because collective ownership of digital platforms and cooperatives can join with prices and choice (Market Socialism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state and corporate power, since encryption and open networks are tools of the people (Civil Libertarianism). The protection of individual rights and expression is the core of the creed, so that people are free to share knowledge and build online (Civil Liberalism). A different global order of fair trade among peoples is sought, because networks should serve communities and not monopoly platforms (Alter-Globalism). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, since the gains of automation belong to all (Progressive Taxation).

Mugabeism.d: Land is taken from large estates and redistributed to the landless peasantry, because the colonial seizure of farmland must be reversed in favour of the black majority (Agrarian Socialism). All peoples of Africa should unite in solidarity against settler and imperial rule, since liberation was won by a continental struggle (Pan-Nationalism). One party dominates the state apparatus and the political process, so that the liberation movement stays in office after independence (Partocracy). A single leader holds absolute personal power for decades, because the father of the nation must guide the revolution without external restraint (Autocracy).

Old Left-Populism.d: The state owns key means of production and directs the economy, because the factories and mines of the nation belong to its working people (State Socialism). Established institutions and gradual change are preferred, since the working class prefers the family, the union hall and the local church to experiments (Conservatism). The nation is defined by shared culture, language and heritage, so that the people are bound by a common home and a common class (Cultural Nationalism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, because a labour party seeks the votes of ordinary people in free elections (Representative Democracy).

Left-State Liberalism.d: Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, because a state that pays for public goods should draw on those with the most (Progressive Taxation). Faith in advance through science and reform guides government, since liberal policy should improve human conditions by design (Progressivism). A single human community with a shared morality beyond nations is the horizon, because every person has equal worth wherever they live (Cosmopolitanism). Global free trade and open borders are welcomed, so that exchange of goods and people spreads prosperity (Globalism). The state steers investment and key sectors with strong directive influence, since public planning secures fair and sustainable growth (Dirigisme). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government, because a unitary administration delivers equal standards to all (Centralism).

American Technocracy.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy by scientific management, because engineers can run industry for the whole population (State Socialism). Cybernetic planning of production by computers and feedback replaces price signals with measurement and energy accounting, so that resources are steered in real time (Cybernetic Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since an energy-based economy of abundance ends the price system (Collective Distribution). Faith in advance through science and reform guides the project, because technical method improves the human condition (Progressivism). Rule by trained specialists chosen for competence governs, since scientists and engineers know how to run a continental economy (Technocracy). The nation rests on shared political values and citizenship, so that the continent's people form one technical unit regardless of origin (Civic Nationalism). The country stays out of foreign entanglements, because North America is self-sufficient (Isolationism). Humanity should gain total mastery over nature and scarcity through technology, since machines can end toil (Prometheanism). The state looks after the health and living conditions of citizens through public provision, because abundance should reach every household (Civic Paternalism). Power is shared between levels of government as regional technical districts, since a continental network is divided into functional areas (Federalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because price and profit waste resources (against Laissez-Faire). Mixed state ownership with private profit is rejected, since it keeps the price system alive (against State Capitalism). One party dominating the state is rejected because politics must give way to technical administration (against Partocracy). Elected representatives governing for voters are rejected since politicians cannot manage engineering problems (against Representative Democracy). All relations resting only on voluntary agreement without coercion are rejected, because social coordination needs scientific control (against Voluntaryism).

Fabian Socialism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy step by step, because gradual public ownership ends exploitation without revolution (State Socialism). The state exerts strong directive influence over investment and key sectors, since expert planning guides industry (Dirigisme). Taxes that rise with income shift the burden toward higher incomes, so that the unearned increment funds public services (Progressive Taxation). Faith in advance through science and reform guides policy, because inevitability of gradualness means steady improvement (Progressivism). Elected representatives govern on behalf of citizens, since the ballot and parliamentary legislation are the path to socialism (Representative Democracy). Rule by trained specialists chosen for competence shapes policy, because research and administration by experts turn ideas into law (Technocracy). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, so that the democratic state is the common instrument (Civic Nationalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common institutions is favoured, since peace and labour standards need joint action (Internationalism). The economy moves toward knowledge and services, because education and research create the new wealth (Post-Industrialism). Ideas and doctrines are judged as tools for improving society, so that whatever works counts as sound (Instrumentalism). The state looks after the health, schooling and housing of citizens, because municipal and national provision secures a national minimum (Civic Paternalism). Town governance by popular assemblies and councils keeps services near the people, since municipal ownership of gas and water is the first step (Municipalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private competition produces poverty and waste (against Laissez-Faire). A revolution that abolishes classes and money at once is rejected, since sudden break risks disorder and reaction (against Communization). Workers' councils of delegates running factories are rejected because expert administration by the state is surer than shop-floor rule (against Councilism).

Ujamaa.d: Land is shared among peasants and farmed in village communities, because familyhood on the land is the African root of socialism (Agrarian Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since every member of the village shares in its work and its harvest (Collective Distribution). Pragmatic reform within the tradition is accepted, so that old extended-family obligations are renewed rather than broken (Progressive Conservatism). One party leads the state and the villages, because a single national movement mobilizes the people (Partocracy). All people of Africa should unite across colonial borders, since African unity is the condition of freedom (Pan-Nationalism). The country avoids alliances and wars abroad, because self-reliance and nonalignment keep the young nation free (Non-Interventionism). Farming and rural settlement are the foundation of society, since the village is the centre of work and life (Agrarianism). The state looks after the education, health and living conditions of citizens, so that public service reaches every village (Civic Paternalism). Historic regions and districts hold their own councils, because local communities must manage their own development (Regionalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since private profit breaks the bonds of the extended family (against Laissez-Faire). A mixed economy of state ownership with private profit is rejected, because it would create classes of exploiters (against State Capitalism). Large-scale manufacturing is rejected since the city factory draws people from the village and breeds inequality (against Industrialism). A revolution of class war is rejected because African socialism rests on familyhood and not on hatred (against Communization).

Bordigism.d: The revolution abolishes money, wages and the state at once, because the new order ends commodity production in a single transformation (Communization). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since a society without exchange replaces buying and selling (Collective Distribution). A single organization of the revolutionary class, the impersonal party, holds leadership of the movement, so that an invariant programme is not diluted by shifting majorities (Partocracy). Cooperation among nations through workers' solidarity across all countries is needed, because the revolution has no national boundary (Internationalism). The belief in one human community without nations comes with it, since class unity replaces national loyalty (Cosmopolitanism). Elected representatives who govern in parliaments are rejected because voting in bourgeois elections only strengthens the existing order (against Representative Democracy). A market left free of regulation is rejected since capital's rule rests on exchange and wage labour (against Laissez-Faire). The nation defined by shared political values and citizenship is rejected, because the proletariat has no fatherland (against Civic Nationalism).

Italian Left Communism.d: Abolition of money, wages and the state in a single stroke is the goal, since the revolution cannot be stopped halfway by a workers' state (Communization). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, because free access to the common product replaces the market (Collective Distribution). The Communist Party of the working class guides the struggle, so that a small organization of conscious militants leads the masses against reformist leaders (Partocracy). Cooperation among workers of all nations, organized in a new international, is required, since the revolution is a world event (Internationalism). Elected representatives and parliamentary participation are rejected because electoral abstention keeps the movement apart from bourgeois democracy (against Representative Democracy). A market free of state control is rejected since the profit system is the root of crisis (against Laissez-Faire).

Juche.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because the people's collective property supports self-reliance (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since the ration and public distribution system feeds every household (Collective Distribution). One party leads the state apparatus under the Korean Workers' leadership, so that the vanguard rules every field of life (Partocracy). The supreme leader holds absolute power as the brain of the people, because the masses become masters of the revolution only through him (Autocracy). The nation is held together by its own culture, language and heritage, since the Korean people carry a distinct tradition (Cultural Nationalism). The country keeps apart from outside powers and trades little, because self-reliance in politics, defence and the economy protects independence (Isolationism). Civilian life is mobilized through military drill and mass campaigns, so that every citizen serves the revolution (Regimentalism). A market free of regulation is rejected since private profit would make the nation dependent on foreign capital (against Laissez-Faire).

Mao Zedong Thought.d: Land is taken from landlords and given to the peasants, because the village poor are the main force of the revolution (Agrarian Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since the people's communes pool grain, labour and tools (Collective Distribution). The Communist Party leads the state and all organizations, so that the mass line from the people through the party back to the people directs the revolution (Partocracy). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private trade revives the old exploiting classes (against Laissez-Faire). Elected representatives governing for competing parties are rejected, since the people's democratic dictatorship does not permit bourgeois parliaments (against Representative Democracy).

Maoism Third Worldism.d: Land is taken from landlords and given to the peasants, because the countryside of the poor nations is where the revolution begins (Agrarian Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since collective distribution ends rural hunger (Collective Distribution). A vanguard party leads a protracted war, so that its leadership holds the army and the villages (Partocracy). A different global order of fair exchange between nations and peoples is sought, because the rich countries live off the labour of the poor world (Alter-Globalism). The expansion of a state's power over other territories is rejected since imperial domination of colonies and the global south is the main enemy (against Imperialism). A market free of regulation is rejected because capital moves wealth from the periphery to the metropolis (against Laissez-Faire). Land is taken from large estates and given to the peasants, because the rural poor are the base of a guerrilla war of liberation. A different global order of fair exchange between nations is sought, since the poor lands must resist the powers that dominate them.

Marxism Leninism Maoism.d: Land is taken from large landowners and given to peasants, because the rural masses are an essential force of every revolution (Agrarian Socialism). Food, housing and tools are shared out by the community to each household according to its needs, since common sharing replaces buying and selling in the people's communes (Collective Distribution). The vanguard party leads the people's war and the new state, so that organized leadership guides the masses through cultural revolution (Partocracy). Cooperation among workers and oppressed peoples of all countries unites the movement, because the revolution is universal (Internationalism). Free enterprise without public intervention is rejected since capitalist property must be expropriated by the people's state and cannot be tolerated beside it (against Laissez-Faire).

Luxemburgism.d: Workers' councils of delegates run factories and neighbourhoods, because the self-activity of the masses, not a party apparatus, builds socialism (Councilism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since socialism means that society provides for all (Collective Distribution). Cooperation among workers of every country is essential, so that the mass strike and solidarity cross borders (Internationalism). The belief in one human community beyond nations belongs to the proletariat, because capitalism is a world system (Cosmopolitanism). A market free of regulation is rejected since the accumulation of capital drives war and misery (against Laissez-Faire). One party dominating the state is rejected because freedom for those who think differently is the lifeblood of socialism, and a ruling clique would stifle it (against Partocracy). Rule by a small elite that governs for its own gain is rejected, since workers must manage their own affairs and not hand them to leaders (against Oligarchy).

Trotskyism.d: The state owns the means of production under workers' control, because the planned economy is the gain of the October revolution that must be defended and extended (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since an economy of abundance ends scarcity (Collective Distribution). A revolutionary party of the working class guides the struggle, so that a disciplined vanguard leads the masses to power (Partocracy). Cooperation among workers of every nation in a new international is required because the permanent revolution cannot be held within a single country (Internationalism). A single human community without nations is the aim, since socialism can be completed only on a world scale (Cosmopolitanism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because capitalism leads to crises and fascism (against Laissez-Faire).

Marxism-Leninism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy through central plans, because public ownership ends exploitation and builds socialism (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since a developed socialist society moves toward distribution without markets (Collective Distribution). A vanguard party organized by democratic centralism leads the state and society, so that the working class has a single guiding organization (Partocracy). Cooperation among workers and socialist states of all countries expresses proletarian solidarity, because the struggle is international (Internationalism). The state steers investment and key sectors with strong directive influence, since planned proportions guide production (Dirigisme). Administrative authority is concentrated in the national government, because a unified state executes the plan across the whole territory (Centralism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since private property in production creates classes (against Laissez-Faire). Elected representatives governing for competing parties are rejected because multiparty parliaments serve the bourgeoisie (against Representative Democracy).

Stalinism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy through five-year plans, because socialism in one country must build heavy industry at a forced pace (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since rationing and public provision replace trade (Collective Distribution). One party dominates the state apparatus and all political activity, so that the party's decisions bind every institution (Partocracy). A single leader holds absolute power without external legal restraints, because the general secretary decides over the party and the police (Autocracy). Large-scale manufacturing, collective farms and giant construction expand material abundance, since industrial power ensures survival (Industrialism). The state absorbs the individual, leaving no private sphere outside party control, because loyalty, family and conscience are subordinated to the cause (Totalism). Authority is concentrated in the capital, which administers every republic through the ministries, since a unitary state enforces the plan (Centralism). All decision-making is concentrated wholly in Moscow, with uniformity suppressing regional autonomy, so that one centre rules the whole union (Hypercentralism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private trade restores capitalism (against Laissez-Faire). Small-scale tools kept to personal creativity and local autonomy are rejected, since decentralized and gentle technology cannot match the power of the large factory (against Convivialism). Splitting territory into seceding units is rejected because the union must remain a single territory (against Patchwork).

Titoism.d: Firms are run by their workers' councils within a market, because self-management gives producers control while competition sets prices (Market Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since socialist solidarity guarantees housing, schooling and care (Collective Distribution). Power is shared between the federation and its republics, so that every nation of the state keeps its own authority (Federalism). The country stays out of the blocs and conflicts of the great powers, because non-alignment protects its independence (Non-Interventionism). The League of Communists leads the state and society, since one party holds the political process together (Partocracy). Profits and rents of public enterprises supply a major share of revenue, because social ownership funds the common budget (State Enterprise Revenue). A market left free of regulation is rejected since private capital would split working people (against Laissez-Faire).

Dengism.d: The state owns and runs major enterprises within a market economy, because socialism with local characteristics uses markets to produce wealth under public control (State Capitalism). One party dominates the state apparatus and the political process, since stability under its leadership is the condition of reform (Partocracy). A path to modernity of its own, outside the dominant Western model, is followed, because opening to the world should happen under national conditions (Alternative Modernism). Foreign policy pursues national interests through power rather than ideology, so that it keeps a low profile and bides its time (Realpolitik). Administrative authority is concentrated in the central government in Beijing, since a unitary state keeps local experiments inside national order (Centralism). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, because all peoples within the borders belong to one country (Civic Nationalism). Profits and rents of state-owned enterprises provide a large part of public revenue, since public ownership funds national development (State Enterprise Revenue).

Hoxhaism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because collective ownership protects a small country from foreign capital (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since socialism guarantees bread and work to all (Collective Distribution). One party leads the state apparatus and the nation, so that its unity guards against revisionism and foreign influence (Partocracy). The country trades little and relies on its own resources, because self-sufficiency keeps out the pressure of both superpowers (Isolationism). Factories, mines and electrification expand material abundance, since industry makes the economy self-reliant (Industrialism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private profit returns foreign dependency (against Laissez-Faire).

Castroism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because revolutionary Cuba put sugar, banks and land in public hands (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since free medicine, schooling and rationing carry equality to every home (Collective Distribution). One party dominates the state apparatus, so that the revolution's leadership guides every organization of the island (Partocracy). The comandante holds absolute personal authority above all institutions, because the historic leader embodies the revolution (Autocracy). The state sends fighters, doctors and aid into other countries, since solidarity with revolutions in Africa and Latin America is a duty of the island (Interventionism). The nation is bound by shared culture and heritage, because the Cuban patriotic tradition of independence gives the revolution its roots (Cultural Nationalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private capital would restore domination by foreign owners (against Laissez-Faire). The expansion of power by large states over other territories is rejected since the empire to the north is the main enemy (against Imperialism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies, especially among the peoples of the south, is pursued, because tricontinental solidarity breaks isolation (Internationalism).

Guevarism.d: Land is taken from large estates and given to the peasants, because the rural poor are the base of a guerrilla war of liberation (Agrarian Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since a new man works for the common good and not for personal gain (Collective Distribution). The armed vanguard intervenes in other countries to spark revolution, because the duty of every revolutionary is to make the revolution wherever oppression exists (Interventionism). Cooperation among workers and peasants of all countries is essential, so that one continental struggle links many fronts (Internationalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since material incentives corrupt the consciousness of the people (against Laissez-Faire).

Cyber-Communism.d: Public ownership of factories, land and banks lets a communist state run the whole economy by algorithm, because machine planning can match supply to need in real time (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since automated abundance makes distribution free of markets (Collective Distribution). Engineers and data scientists chosen for competence run the planning models, so that technical expertise and not party rhetoric guides the plan (Technocracy). Humanity should gain total mastery over nature and scarcity through robots and artificial intelligence, because automation can free everyone from toil forever (Prometheanism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies is needed, since a planetary network of planning crosses borders (Internationalism). Information systems replace markets by feedback, so that production and stocks are steered by live data and not by prices (Cybernetic Socialism). Free enterprise and private trade are rejected because price signals cannot coordinate a world of automated abundance without public intervention (against Laissez-Faire).

De Leonism.d: Workers organize in industrial unions that take over the economy and its workplaces, because the union is the form in which the working class manages production (Syndicalism). Industrial unions send delegates to a congress that replaces the political state, since representation by workplace and industry instead of district gives producers government (Syndicracy). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, so that the cooperative commonwealth ends wage labour (Collective Distribution). Factories and mills expand material abundance, because the full development of industry is the base of socialism (Industrialism). Cooperation among workers of every country is part of one union movement, since capitalist power is global (Internationalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because the capitalist class lives on the unpaid labour of workers (against Laissez-Faire).

Marxism-Kemalism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because the republic's national revolution is carried forward by public ownership (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since the working people of the nation share its output (Collective Distribution). The nation rests on citizenship and shared political values, so that every labourer of the republic belongs to the people regardless of descent (Civic Nationalism). One party leads the state apparatus, because a vanguard of republican cadres guides the revolution (Partocracy). Factories and railways expand material abundance, since an industrial base frees the country from imperialism (Industrialism). Rule by religious clergy under divine law is rejected because a secular republic must free workers from clerical authority (against Theocracy).

National Communism.d: The state owns the means of production and directs the economy, because public ownership lets the country build socialism in its own way (State Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since socialist provision shares output among the people (Collective Distribution). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, so that working women and peasants gain full rights (Social-Progressivism). One party dominates the state apparatus, because the party of the nation leads the revolution (Partocracy). The nation is bound by shared culture, language and heritage, since the people's own tradition shapes its road to socialism (Cultural Nationalism). Foreign policy pursues the country's interests through power and not through ideology, because independence from Moscow's direction demands cold calculation (Realpolitik). Factories and heavy industry expand material abundance, since an industrial base secures sovereignty (Industrialism). The state looks after the health, housing and schooling of citizens, because welfare binds the people to the regime (Civic Paternalism). Public etiquette and discipline are enforced, so that order marks the socialist nation (Disciplinarianism). Authority is concentrated in the national government, which treats districts as administrative units, because a unitary state executes the plan (Centralism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since private capital serves foreign interests (against Laissez-Faire). A single human community beyond nations is rejected because the national road must not be subordinated to a world centre (against Cosmopolitanism). Public life shaped by revealed doctrine is rejected, since the party stands for a secular outlook (against Religious Traditionalism). Rule by clergy under divine law is rejected because the church must not govern (against Theocracy).

Libertarian Municipalism.d: Citizens govern their town through popular assemblies, because power should rest in face-to-face municipal councils and not in remote capitals (Municipalism). Communal living and shared ownership at the local level give people direct control of their economy, since the commune is the cell of a free society (Communalism). Production and exchange are managed voluntarily without hierarchy or state, so that a stateless socialism grows from municipal life (Free Socialism). Balancing prosperity with ecological health, since social hierarchy lies behind the destruction of nature, is needed (Environmentalism). Towns join in a union of sovereign communes that coordinate by delegates, because a network of confederated municipalities replaces the nation-state (Confederalism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since neighbourhood bonds give people belonging (Communitarianism). Cooperation among nations and peoples by their free federations is pursued, because municipal movements are linked across borders (Internationalism). Concentrated authority in a national government is rejected since central administration drains the power of the commune (against Centralism). Complete concentration of power in the capital is rejected because it destroys the people's own assemblies (against Hypercentralism).

Communalism.d: Communes of free citizens own land and industry in common, because shared ownership at the local level gives every member a voice in the economy (Communalism). Communes join in a federation by agreement, so that the union of free communities replaces rule by a single capital (Confederalism). A stateless, voluntary socialism grows without hierarchy, since cooperation needs no ruler (Free Socialism). Balancing prosperity with ecological health is needed because the commune lives in harmony with the land it shares (Environmentalism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since neighbours depend on one another (Communitarianism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, so that common stores provide for all members (Collective Distribution). Citizens vote directly on laws through referendums and assemblies, because the commune's members decide for themselves (Referendum Democracy). Town governance by popular assemblies keeps authority near the people, since the neighbourhood is the school of citizenship (Municipalism). Concentrated authority in a national government is rejected because a distant capital cannot know local needs (against Centralism). Rule by a small elite that governs for its own gain is rejected since commune assemblies are open to all members (against Oligarchy).

Minarcho-Socialism.d: The state is limited to a minimal night-watchman role, because a free society of workers needs government only to guard against force and fraud (Minarchism). A voluntary socialism without hierarchy or coercion organizes production, since workplaces owned by their members can be built from below (Free Socialism). The country avoids alliances and wars abroad, so that its small state spends nothing on foreign adventures (Non-Interventionism). Workplaces belong to those who work in them, and a small public body guards contracts and common defence, because no large apparatus of rule is needed when producers own their tools.

Libertarian Socialism.d: Production and exchange are managed voluntarily without hierarchy or coercion, because freedom and cooperation are the same thing (Free Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since free access to the common product replaces wages (Collective Distribution). Workers' councils of delegates run factories and neighbourhoods, so that those who do the work decide (Councilism). Rule is abolished and replaced by voluntary association, because power corrupts every ruler (Anarchism). Cooperation among workers of every country is essential, since solidarity needs no state to enforce it (Internationalism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against authority, because liberty is the first principle of socialism (Civil Libertarianism). Workplaces are run through councils of workers and consumers who plan together, since participatory planning replaces both markets and bosses (Participatory Economics). One party dominating the state is rejected because a ruling party reproduces hierarchy (against Partocracy). The absorption of the person into the state is rejected since no authority may own individuals (against Totalism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because wage labour and private ownership are forms of domination (against Laissez-Faire).

Council Communism.d: Abolition of money, wages and the state is the goal, because the working class can only free itself by sweeping away the whole wage system (Communization). Workers' councils of delegates run factories and neighbourhoods, since the self-organized masses, not a party, hold power (Councilism). Goods and services are distributed by the community to everyone according to need, since free access to the common product ends wages and pay (Collective Distribution). Cooperation among workers of every country is essential because capital is international (Internationalism). One party dominating the state is rejected since a party leadership would become a new ruling class (against Partocracy). State ownership and central planning of the economy are rejected because the state would only replace private bosses with officials who own the means of production (against State Socialism). Elected representatives governing in parliaments are rejected, since electoral politics keeps workers passive (against Representative Democracy). An economy free of government intervention is rejected, since private transactions for profit let capital exploit wage labour (against Laissez-Faire). Rule by a small elite or ruling class that governs for its own gain is rejected, since the councils' delegates stay recallable and accountable to workers (against Oligarchy).

Democratic Confederalism.d: Communes of citizens share ownership and decisions locally, because self-governing villages and neighbourhoods are the base of a free society (Communalism). Communes join in a federation by agreement, so that peoples of different origins coordinate without a state above them (Confederalism). Balancing prosperity with ecological health is needed, since an ecological society is part of its aims (Environmentalism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, because women, youth and neighbours hold common responsibilities (Communitarianism). A voluntary socialism without hierarchy organizes work, since cooperatives and councils free production (Free Socialism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand gender equality, because women's liberation is the measure of freedom (Social-Progressivism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded, since pluralist rights limit every authority (Civil Libertarianism). Workplaces are run by councils of workers and consumers, so that economic planning is participatory (Participatory Economics). Coexisting communities with their own languages and faiths are recognized, because peoples of many origins share the same land (Multiculturalism). Small-scale tools that serve personal creativity and local autonomy are favoured, since a gentle, decentralized technology keeps control with communities (Convivialism). Concentrated authority in a national government is rejected because the nation-state is the root of oppression (against Centralism). Complete concentration of power in the capital is rejected, since a uniform state suppresses regional self-rule (against Hypercentralism). Rule by a small elite that governs for its own gain is rejected because everyone takes part in decisions (against Oligarchy).

Guild Socialism.d: Each trade is run by a self-governing national guild of its workers that bargains with the state on behalf of consumers, because craftsmen know their own work and should hold it as a public trust (Guild Socialism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, since fellowship in the guild and the town belongs to a humane order (Communitarianism). An economy free of government intervention and regulation is rejected, since private transactions for profit turn labour into a commodity (against Laissez-Faire). Consumers are represented through the community's own councils, while the guilds guarantee the quality of work and the dignity of the craftsman. Industries are run by worker guilds in a reciprocal relationship with a state, so that each craft governs its own work.

Eco-Socialism.d: Balancing prosperity with environmental health through regulation and public control is essential, because capital's endless growth destroys the biosphere (Environmentalism). Nature and wild ecosystems have intrinsic value and deserve protection, since the earth is a commons and not a resource of the rich (Conservationism). A voluntary, stateless and free socialism without hierarchy organizes production for use, so that cooperation replaces the profit motive (Free Socialism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since a society that shares its output consumes within planetary limits (Collective Distribution). Communes own land and shared resources in common as one local community, because commune members who live on the land protect its ecosystems (Communalism). Cooperation among nations through treaties and common bodies answers climate change, since warming crosses borders (Internationalism). An economy free of government intervention and regulation is rejected, since private transactions for profit drive pollution (against Laissez-Faire). Large-scale manufacturing is rejected since fossil-fuelled industry degrades the planet (against Industrialism).

Cybersyn Socialism.d: Rule by trained specialists chosen for competence guides production, because engineers can coordinate a large economy with data (Technocracy). Humanity should gain mastery over nature and scarcity through computers and automation, so that factories run themselves under shared management (Prometheanism). Goods and services are allocated by the community according to need, since a planned economy with real-time information ends shortages (Collective Distribution). Faith in advance through science and reform guides the project, because rational design of the economy improves human conditions (Progressivism). The state owns and directs key industries, since nationalized firms are linked through a telex network to the centre (State Socialism). Workers share in the profits and decisions of firms through participation, so that factory committees keep control in the hands of labour (Yellow Socialism). A market left free of regulation is rejected because private capital must not steer the economy (against Laissez-Faire).

Fourierism.d: Idealistic model communities in phalansteries show a better society, because voluntary association and example can persuade where force fails (Utopian Socialism). Settlements share labour, housing and meals in common, since communal living lets passions work in harmony (Communalism). Society is a community of mutual obligation, so that members are bound by shared enjoyment of work (Communitarianism). Consensual adult conduct and the passions are left free, because the natural attractions of people should not be repressed by moral law (Permissivism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since the liberation of women measures social progress (Social-Progressivism). A market left free of regulation is rejected since competition and commerce produce waste and misery (against Laissez-Faire).

Gandhian Socialism.d: Society is a community of mutual obligation, because village life rests on service, trusteeship and self-restraint (Communitarianism). The country avoids alliances and wars abroad, since a nation of nonviolent people has no need for foreign adventures (Non-Interventionism). Dismantling machine-driven industry in favour of hand spinning and village crafts keeps work human, so that technology does not replace labour (Neo-Luddism). Productive property, especially land, is spread among many households, since village republics of small owners resist concentration (Distributism). Land is shared among peasants and tilled in common, because the village poor are the backbone of the nation (Agrarian Socialism). Large-scale manufacturing is rejected because heavy industry enslaves the people and exploits the villages (against Industrialism). Concentrated authority in a national government is rejected since power should rest in self-governing village councils (against Centralism). Opposing war and militarism is a duty, because truth and nonviolence are the only lasting means (Pacifism). Small, repairable tools that serve personal creativity and local autonomy are preferred, so that the spinning wheel stays in every home (Convivialism). Order is kept by peer accountability and community ostracism instead of police, since the village conscience is a stronger guardian than the state (Reputationalism).

Scythianism.d: Land is held and tilled in common by the peasantry, because the Russian village commune has an older socialism than any imported doctrine (Agrarian Socialism). Social identity and loyalty are anchored in a great Eurasian civilization, since the Scythian steppe stands apart from the old Europe (Civilizationism). A path to modernity of its own, outside the dominant Western model, is chosen so that the revolution breaks with the past in a new way (Alternative Modernism). Rule driven by the mass passions of the uprising is accepted, because the elemental storm of the people sweeps away the old order (Ochlocracy).

Proutism.d: A single human community with a shared morality beyond nations is the horizon, because spiritual unity of all beings transcends national borders (Cosmopolitanism). Nature and wild ecosystems are protected, since all living things share the same cosmic life (Conservationism). A union of sovereign regions formed by agreement ties together socioeconomic zones, so that each area decides its own economy (Confederalism). Faith in advance through science and reform guides the spiritual and material progress of society, because human development is the goal of life (Progressivism).

Geolibertarianism.d: Land is taxed on its unimproved site value, because the rent of nature belongs to all and replaces every other tax (Land Value Tax). An economy free of government intervention lets owners trade, since the single land tax leaves earnings untouched (Laissez-Faire). The protection of individual rights and expression is the aim, so that each person owns themselves (Civil Liberalism). The state is limited to protecting rights and collecting ground rent, because it should do nothing else (Minarchism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, since self-ownership forbids arbitrary rule (Civil Libertarianism). The country avoids alliances and wars abroad, because commerce and peace go together (Non-Interventionism). State ownership with central planning is rejected since it denies both self-ownership and the fair claim of all to land (against State Socialism).

Social Libertarianism.d: A basic income within a capitalist economy gives each person a guaranteed share, because a fair start makes liberty real (Basic Income Capitalism). Land is taxed on its unimproved site value, since the community's claim on natural resources funds the dividend (Land Value Tax). The state is limited to a minimal role, so that coercion goes no further than protecting rights and providing the dividend (Minarchism). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, because freedom of the person is inviolable (Civil Libertarianism). Government acts to remedy discrimination and expand equality, since social justice and liberty support one another (Social-Progressivism).

Helvetic Model.d: Citizens vote directly on laws and policies through referendums and initiatives, because the Swiss people keep sovereignty at the ballot box (Referendum Democracy). Cantons form a union by agreement, so that each member remains a state with its own constitution (Confederalism). Power is shared between the federal government and the cantons, since subsidiarity keeps authority close to the citizen (Federalism). The country keeps a militia defence while staying out of alliances, because armed neutrality has protected its independence (Armed Neutrality). Personal privacy, free speech and due process are guarded against state power, so that civic rights bind every level of government (Civil Libertarianism). Rule by a small elite that governs for its own gain is rejected because the people's right of veto checks any ruling group (against Oligarchy).

Minarcho-Distributism.d: Productive property is spread among many households, because widespread ownership of land and tools keeps families free of both banks and the state (Distributism). A market of small owners exchanging voluntarily secures that spread, since free trade among proprietors prevents monopoly (Free Market Distributism). The state is limited to a minimal role, so that it protects property and contracts and nothing more (Minarchism).
